The series' name is a joke about a boy band and a word for a neighborhood, and the first week is the neighborhood as a crowd: more heads than you can count, pressed into one square.

The lines change their job as the months go by. In the first week they pile up until a square is full: a crowd of toothy heads, a figure with wings, two black bodies edged in neon. In January they thin out, and a whole scene can be a few white strokes on purple. By June a figure is one black shape with a white edge, standing alone in a grey room. The crowd of December is a crowd of grins. The figures of June are alone, and one of them holds a bird.

From the start the series was given away as much as sold. On December 14 the artist posted the tenth work and said it had been dropped straight into the wallets of the people who had bought the earlier ones. The first five works in the series went to Jamie Thingelstad on August 14, 2022, hours after he bought the origin piece of the Faces, and three of those five hang here. Then on October 16, the day after the series ended, the artist sent him the rest. Count the faces in each work as you go. The room begins with more than you can count and ends with one figure and one bird.

Six works from December 8 to 12, 2021, including the very first New Nifty on the Block. The square is packed every time. Three of these were among the five the artist sent the collector in August 2022, before the rest of the series followed.

The first work in the series: a crowd of heads and raised limbs on cyan, drawn in red, blue, white and yellow scribble over black outline. Teeth are everywhere, in a skull at the top, a grinning head at the left, a jaw at the bottom edge. A hand with spread fingers reaches up at the upper left. Nothing is in front of anything else; the figures share one weave, and a face found in it is lost again as soon as the eye moves. It was drawn on December 8, 2021, seven weeks after the artist's first ink, and it announces a neighborhood: everyone on the block at once, all teeth, all waving. On October 15, 2022, the last day of the series, the artist drew it again, and that version hangs in the last room of the wing.
A green-faced figure with ex eyes sits cross-legged in an orange body with two yellow wings spread behind it, on a ground of white, magenta and black strokes.

Two figures lean together on a pink and orange ground, one with yellow hair, both with round eyes and red mouths, and between them a large red heart. Two smaller hearts float at the sides. The bodies are drawn in green, yellow and white scribble with a thin white edge, and the big heart is outlined in white like a badge. It is the first drawing in the series with a heart in it, and with 378 recorded strokes the most worked in this room. Two people and a heart between them is as plain as a picture gets, and the artist drew it in the first week, before the masks, before the crash, when the block was new and everyone on it was a friend.

Two black figures edged in white and pink stand against a dark ground of colored scribble, one with an X in its eye and the other with a Y, a hand of three pink fingers between them. The collector bought it on October 14, 2022, two days before the whole series arrived.
One big face: two round red eyes with green X marks, a blue square eye between them, a mouth of white teeth, and thick swirls of red, blue and yellow line around the edge.

Mid December. The figures line up. Seven robed figures in a row, three lumpy ones side by side, a row of ghosts over black grass. The second of them, number 10, is the one the artist announced as a pocket drop for earlier buyers.

A purple mass with four faces in it, each with a grin of white teeth and small yellow eyes, drawn in white line over an olive grid; the artist dropped it free into the wallets of the people who had bought the earlier works, and said so.

Seven tall figures stand in a row, their bodies long stripes of blue, green, pink and yellow, their round heads burning with orange and red scribble. Each face has two small eyes and a grin. The heads touch a band of fire along the top, so the row seems to stand under one burning roof. It is the first row of figures in the series, and the tallest. Seven people in a line with their hair on fire, grinning: it is a band, or a lineup, or a block of neighbors standing outside a house that is burning, and pleased about it. In December 2021 that was what the market felt like from inside.
Three lumpy figures in orange and blue scribble stand side by side on black, each with yellow eyes and a wide grin of white teeth.

Six ghosts hang in a row under a pink sky, their long bodies drawn in thin blue, yellow and white lines that fall like rain, their faces screaming. Black grass stands up along the bottom in white outline. Three days after the row of seven burning heads, the row is back, but the fire has gone out: the heads are pale ovals with dark eyes and open mouths, and the bodies are see-through. Set the two rows together and the series has already found its two moods in its second week. The same lineup, grinning on Thursday and screaming on Sunday.
January and February 2022. The lines loosen and multiply, and the figures are harder to find. One hangs upside down behind bars.
A tangle of blue, orange and black line over olive and red, with two grinning heads at the top corners and a white line running around the edge like a frame.

A group of figures drawn in white, green and orange line on purple, their arms raised. One at the center has a dark face and both hands up. Twenty-nine recorded strokes make the whole drawing, and nothing is filled in; the purple shows through every body. It is the sparest crowd in the room, and the first where the line is nearly all that there is. Hands up can be a cheer or a surrender. On January 20, 2022, with the market sliding, the drawing does not say which.
A figure hangs upside down behind five dark red bars on a red ground, its skull at the bottom with teeth showing, its legs crossed at the top, the first prisoner in the series.
A figure in blue, orange and green scribble sits in a chair at a window, on pink, with a second small figure standing on the sill at the upper left.
One week in March. Four drawings that are each a scene or a character, with the line now doing the describing.
A cartoon scene on teal and pink: three smiling faces in a box of yellow dots, a round green tree with a face, a yellow snail with antennae, and pink clouds along the top.
A group of figures in white and yellow line on orange, a grinning monkey at the left and four others with round heads, over a ground of colored bars.
A figure with square glasses and a wide grin crosses its arms, drawn in black, white and green hatching over an orange ground, spikes of hair standing up.
A figure with a huge round head dances with one arm up and one out, drawn in red, white and blue line on dark teal, its face a swirl with a small grin.
After nine weeks, four works from May 30 to June 3. A crowd of yellow characters in Nifty Ink shirts, then two figures alone in grey rooms, then a pair with red heads.

A crowd of yellow characters with spiky hair on pale blue, the one in front wearing sunglasses and a white tee that says NIFTY INK, pale faces floating behind them: the block in its uniform, two weeks after the crash.

A black figure in a suit stands in a grey room, drawn with a thin white edge, its head stretched sideways like a balloon with two ex eyes on it. A single yellow flower grows at the lower right. Thirty recorded strokes. In December the black figures were edged in neon and surrounded by scribble; here the same black body stands in nothing at all, and the room is empty except for the flower. It was drawn on May 31, 2022, at the end of the month the market fell. The suit, the grey walls and the cancelled eyes say what kind of month it was. The flower says the drawing is not finished with hope.

A tall black figure with a white edge stands at the right of a grey room and holds out its arm, and on its hand sits a small purple bird with a yellow beak. The figure's face has two spiral eyes and a row of teeth. A darker square is drawn on the wall behind it. The bird is the one colored thing in the picture, and the whole arm is drawn to carry it. The day before, the figure in the suit stood in the same grey room with a flower it did not touch. This one has reached out and something has landed. Of all the works in the first half of the series, it is the one that most plainly says what the artist wanted from the block: not the crowd, but one small thing, alive, that comes to the hand.

Two figures with red heads and black hair stand on a yellow ground ruled with white lines, a red heart between them and X marks on their faces, six months after the hearts of December, and the heart is broken down the middle.

Go back to the first work and then to the figure with the bird. Both are made of line. One has more faces than you can count and fills the square to the corners; the other has one face, one arm and one small bird, and most of the square is empty wall. In December the artist was drawing a crowd to join. By June the crowd had thinned to one, and what it had left was something small and alive to hold out. The room is the distance between them.

Two kinds of body share this room. One is a skeleton: a stick figure of bones, drawn in a few colored lines, dancing or walking on a flat ground. The other is a monster: a hunched, furred or armored creature in the dark, with fangs. Twenty works, from New Year's Day 2022 to June 3. The skeletons are the series at play. The monsters are what it drew when it stopped playing.

The skeletons are all limbs. Their arms and legs bend at too many joints, their hands are spread like rakes, and their heads are small skulls with teeth. Most of them wear something: a jacket, a tutu, a hat. They are dead and they are dancing, and the joke never wears out. The monsters are all mass. They crouch, they fill the square, and the light picks out teeth and eyes and leaves the rest in shadow. The artist painted them with the care the skeletons never asked for, and the care is where the dread comes from.

This is also the room where the collecting began. Jamie Thingelstad's first purchase from the series was the skeleton that opens it, the horned figure in a jacket from New Year's Day, bought on May 1, 2022, for twenty xDai. Four days later he bought the blue bull walking through fire. The two kinds do not alternate neatly. Watch the stick figures loosen through February, then see the monsters take over in April and May, until the last work is a creature hanging in a dark forest.
Three stick figures from the first three days of 2022, then the first monster at the end of the month. The first of them became the collector's first purchase from the series.

A horned figure in a jacket stands square on an olive ground, drawn in black with a cream fill, its ribs showing through the coat like a fossil. Thin red and yellow lines wander over the whole square in loose rectangles, as if a second drawing had been laid on the first. The hands are two rakes of fingers. The year 2022 begins with this work, made in the morning of January 1, and four months later it began something else: on May 1, 2022, it was the first New Nifty on the Block that Jamie Thingelstad bought, for twenty xDai, seventeen days after his first n n x y z purchase of any kind. A skeleton in a jacket, standing its ground with its ribs showing, was the one he chose first.
A stick figure in a pink tutu stands on one leg like a pole, arms out, its head a ball of red scribble with two round eyes.
A lanky figure in blue and orange line dances on teal, one arm raised high in a loop, its small skull grinning with white fangs.

A skeleton painted in dark purple and grey emerges from black, its skull tilted toward you, its ribcage open, one hand held up with the fingers spread. Light catches the top of the skull, the knuckles and the edges of the ribs, and everything else sinks into the ground. It is the first painted body in the room, and the first with no color at all beyond the purple of the bone. The stick skeletons of the first week were dancing. This one has stopped, turned, and raised a hand, and the raised hand is the whole difference: a joke about death, painted with enough care, is no longer a joke.
Eight works in three weeks. Skeletons put on hats and cowboy boots, and between them the monsters arrive, one with fangs and one with a grin.

A hunched creature with a long skull, a red mouth of white fangs and two red eyes crouches in grey light, its fur drawn in a halo of black and white scratches. Four days after the purple skeleton, the painted body is back, but furred, with hands planted on the ground and a spine of spikes down its back. The dark around it is not flat; it is made of soft grey discs, like a fog. The mouth is the only red thing, and it is open. It is the first monster in the series that is plainly angry, and it arrived on February 2, 2022, with nothing in the record to explain it except the drawing itself.
Two skeletons in yellow and pink line meet on orange, one bending low and the other reaching down, their skulls grinning with white fangs.
A skeleton in a tall yellow hat stands on teal, its boxy body striped with pink, red and yellow, both arms held out and its ribs drawn in white.
A cowboy skeleton strides to the left on orange, hat tipped, one leg raised, its chest a box of blue and red scribble with a heart in it.
A hunched figure in yellow, pink and blue scribble crouches on olive, its boxy head open at the front with two staring eyes and a row of teeth.
A purple figure with a round head and a wide grin of white teeth holds out its arms in the dark, its eyes two red X marks, the grin and the cancelled eyes together for the first time in the room.
March and April. A moth, a crowned skeleton on a maze, a horned creature, and two more cowboys, one dancing on red and one walking downhill.

A moth with wings of gold and black stripes spreads them across a purple ground, its small red face at the top with two antennae. The body is a stack of striped segments, and the wings are drawn in long curved strokes that follow their shape. Two round tips hang below like feet. It is the one winged creature in the room, and the most carefully built, with 380 recorded strokes. It was made on March 2, 2022, the day the artist posted a list of reasons for loving Nifty Ink: easy and fun, works without problems, no cost to mint, a nice and active community. The moth is that mood with wings on. It is also drawn to a lamp.
A horned creature made of colored scribble crouches on all fours in the dark, two round eyes and a mouth of white fangs in its square head.
A cowboy skeleton dances on red, one arm up and one out, white lines of motion curving around it and three white squiggles rising from its hat.
A metallic figure with red ex eyes walks down a black slope on lime green, its body drawn in grey and blue with white highlights.
The last four works, from April 25 to June 3, are all monsters, and all painted. The skeletons are gone. The second of them, the bull, was bought the day it was drawn.

A blob of a monster fills the square from the black, its mouth a cave of white teeth, its two eyes on stalks with orange lids. The body is drawn in green and brown with scribble over it, and a hand at the upper right holds up a small round thing. In February a purple figure grinned with a row of teeth; here the grin has become the whole body, and the eyes have left the head. It was drawn on April 25, 2022, the same day as the two cats with a heart between them in the room next door, and the same day the artist gave the collector the drawing that marked two hundred inks. One hand and one day made a love note and this.

A blue bull with small horns walks through orange fire, its back and legs drawn in blue and green scribble, a bouquet of smoke rising from its tail; the collector bought it on May 5, 2022, the day after it was drawn, for fifteen xDai, four days before the market fell.
A furry creature with a huge mane of colored strokes grins with white fangs, one red eye showing, on a ground of yellow circles.

A hunched creature with long hair and long thin arms hangs in a dark forest, drawn in black and gold strokes between tall black tree trunks, the sky behind it burning orange. Its face looks down and is barely there. The hands reach toward the ground. It is the last work in the room, made June 3, 2022, and the only one where the monster has a place to be: a forest, with trees and a sky, and the sky is on fire. After five months of skeletons that danced and monsters that roared, the series ends its first part with a creature that has gone quiet and is looking at the ground. Whatever the fire behind it is, it has turned its back on it.

Look again at the first skeleton, standing square in its jacket on New Year's Day, and then at the creature hanging in the forest in June. The one is all bone and line on a flat ground, and it is a joke about being dead. The other is all hair and shadow in a place with trees, and it is not a joke. The room walked from one to the other in five months, and the collector's first two purchases from the series, the New Year skeleton and the bull in the fire, stand at the two ends of the walk.

This room is painted. The marks are soft, broad and blended, and the line, when it appears, sits on top of color instead of making it. Twenty-four works from the first six months of the series, December 2021 to June 2022, hang here because they share that surface, and because they are the works where the artist let the drawing be beautiful without a joke in it.

What is painted changes from week to week. A dancer and a duck in a room, a sunset over water on Christmas Eve, a sky of pale cloud, a house in a field, a figure in a yellow raincoat, a woman wrapped in cloth, a rooster, an elephant, a mouse. Between them come color fields with no subject at all: drips, stripes, a plaid of black and red. The artist's handle on every platform began with four zeros, and the bio line read born readymade to please the eye. This is the room where that line is simply true.

In most of the series the ground is flat color. Here it is air, cloud, light and weather, and the figures stand in it, not on it. The astronaut, the most anxious face in the room, was the collector's fourth purchase from the series, bought on May 25, 2022, the day it was drawn. The barn full of figures that closes the room is the last work of the series' first part, made June 4, 2022, four days before the masks began.

Four works from the first three weeks. Faces float in soft light, a dancer and a duck share a room, and the first color field and the first landscape arrive. The first of them was among the five works the artist sent the collector in August 2022.

Faces float in pink and gold light, drawn as thin blue and yellow outlines over a ground of soft overlapping discs. Six of them hang at the left and the top like balloons, each with two round eyes and a mouth, and a profile with spiky hair stands in the middle looking right. The whole picture glows, and nothing in it is solid. It was made on December 8, 2021, the same day as the first two works in the series, and it is the first painted one. On the first day the artist drew a crowd of teeth, a winged figure, and this: faces as light, pleased and weightless. It was one of the five earliest works sent to the collector on August 14, 2022.

A dancer in a short gold dress raises her arms and shouts, and beside her a duck in a feathered coat stands with its wings folded, under a hooked lamp. Both are painted in gold and brown with scribble over them, and the room behind them is a weave of pink, lilac and gold lines. The dancer's face is red with a wide open mouth; the duck's eyes are narrow and its beak is shut. It is the most peopled painting in the room, with 562 recorded strokes. One of them is having the time of her life and the other has seen it all before, and the picture is funny because it will not say which of them is right.
No figure at all: vertical drips of orange, red, blue, white and brown run down the square, crossed by a few white and red lines.

A sunset over water. Pale cloud at the top, a band of orange and gold at the horizon, and below it a winding channel of blue water between dark purple and green banks, painted in soft overlapping strokes with scribble on top. It is the first landscape in the series, made on Christmas Eve 2021, and the most densely drawn work in the room. Nothing in it grins. For one evening in the first month, the block was a river and a sky, and the artist, who would spend the next year drawing teeth, drew the light going down over water and signed it.
January and February 2022. A cloudy sky, a house in a field, and three color fields in a row, then a figure in a raincoat.
A sky of pale cloud, painted in cream, blue and pink discs with yellow light coming through the middle and thin blue and red lines drawn over the clouds.
A house with a pitched roof drawn in brown and lime green line, standing in a field of olive and blue strokes under a sky of blue bars.
On cream: a red block, a white block, a grey ring with a black center, a blue box hanging from a line, a magenta block, and three small green flowers on stems.

A figure in a yellow raincoat with the hood up stands against dark green, its face in shadow under the hood except for a red mouth of pointed teeth and two red marks for eyes. The coat is painted in broad yellow strokes with white lines for the seams. One sleeve ends in a hand drawn in white and red. The figure fills the right half of the square and faces left into the dark. The coat is cheerful and the face inside it is not. It is the first time in the series that something bright is worn over something with teeth, and the masks of the summer will do it a hundred more times.
March and April. A creature in a field of light, trees in a haze, a gown, a wrapped woman, a rooster and an elephant.
A black creature with a striped head and a white grin crouches in a field of gold and purple discs, its spotted tail curling up behind it and a hand reaching out.
Trees in a haze of pale discs, drawn in thin blue, green and white line, a tall trunk at the center and grass at the bottom in loops.
A figure in a huge brown gown turns away on olive, its arms a flurry of orange and black strokes, a spray of colored dots rising from it like confetti.

A woman with black hair in a bun and a small pale face stands wrapped in cloth: blue and pink bands wound across her chest, and a long striped robe of gold, brown and purple falling to the bottom edge. The ground is dark olive and flat. Her mouth is a small red mark and her eyes are two short lines. It is the stillest work in the room, and the only one that looks like a dressed person seen from the front. Her eyes are closed, or nearly. In a series where every face is turned to the viewer and most of them are shouting, she is the one who is not available, and the drawing respects that.
A rooster painted in red, purple and blue feathers stands on blue, its yellow beak open, a white belly and a raised crest of spikes.
An elephant with a curled trunk and small round eyes sits on yellow, its hide painted in grey and purple with scribble over it, flames rising from its head and tail.
The last nine works, May 4 to June 4. An angel in the clouds, an astronaut the collector bought the day it was drawn, a mouse, a figure in a hat, a gold armored body, and a barn full of figures.
A creature with a halo kneels in a bank of clouds under a gold sun, its head bowed and its hands raised, painted in brown and gold with white light on the edges, five days before the crash.

An astronaut's head inside a round helmet, against black space full of white stars. The face is painted in soft gold and grey discs, with two mismatched eyes, a long nose and a grimace of teeth drawn in orange line. The helmet is a white ring with grey reflections. The face is the most anxious in the room: one eye wide, the other narrowed, the mouth pulled down at the corners. It was drawn on May 25, 2022, and Jamie Thingelstad bought it within hours for fifteen xDai, his fourth from the series. Two weeks after the market fell, a face sealed inside a helmet, far from everything, worried: it is easy to see why a collector who had just arrived on the board chose it.
A mouse with round ears, black button eyes and whiskers hugs its own pink arms on a yellow ground inside a black frame, painted in gold, orange and pink.
A figure in a wide-brimmed hat with flowers on it, seen from the side, its face a blur of pale grey and pink discs against white and blue haze, drawn almost entirely in translucent strokes.
A gold armored body with two round yellow eyes and a grin of white teeth stands in a frame, its plates drawn in short strokes of gold, blue and white over black.
A figure with a mass of dark red hair over its face holds a hand to its head, in a yellow shirt on a ground of yellow bars, the face hidden entirely.

Figures hang and climb in the rafters of a barn, painted in brown and gold over a ground of tall vertical strokes. One with a long face hangs from a beam at the right, two more sit on a shelf at the upper right, and a grinning head looks out from the lower corner. The whole picture is made of uprights, beams, legs and falling strokes. It is the last work of New Nifty on the Block's first part, made June 4, 2022. The crowd of the first week has come indoors and climbed into the dark, and the one face that looks out is grinning. Four days later the series began drawing masks and did almost nothing else for ten weeks.

The first painting has faces floating in pink light, and nothing in it has an edge. The last has figures hanging in a barn made of boards. The soft ground is still there in both. What changed is that the figures found something to hold on to, and that the thing they hold on to is a beam, in a barn, in the dark. The gentlest room in the wing ends on the edge of the summer of masks.

A head drawn as a box, with boxes inside it. That is the mask of this room: square eyes holding spirals, targets or crosses, a mouth drawn as a grille of upright bars, and every corner of the square filled with zigzag, beads and scribble. Twenty-four works, from June 8 to August 19, 2022. For ten weeks that summer nearly everything the artist drew was a mask, and this room holds the squarest of them.

The parts are a kit. An eye can be a red X in a box, a spiral in a box, a flower, a planet with a ring. A mouth can be white blocks, a row of fangs, a bar of grey teeth. Beads run along the edges, zigzags run along the brows, and a few tubes stand up on top like hair or a crown. Each mask is a new arrangement of the same parts, and the pleasure of the room is watching one mind play the same game twenty-four times without repeating a move. A mask is a face with the person taken out. These have the person's attention left in.

The summer had a shape outside the drawings too. In June the artist minted 300 nifties, the milestone piece, into the collector's wallet and dozens of others. In July the cats from the spring became a club of nearly ten thousand on Polygon. On August 11 the artist announced that the inks would be burned, every unsold copy, and the masks drawn after that date carry a price in the post that announced them: five of five, fifteen xDai. The last mask in the room, the long yellow face behind a cage of lines, was drawn on the last day of the mask summer, and it is the first in the room that looks like someone.

The first eight masks, June 8 to 25. Every one is filled edge to edge, and the X and the spiral trade places from eye to eye. On June 20 the artist marked three hundred inks on the board with a drawing minted free into the collector's wallet and many others; the masks went on the next day.

The first mask of the summer: a red X in a yellow box on the left, a purple cross in a box on the right, a band of dark red beads across the brow, and a long white zigzag under them like a row of teeth. Below that, white boxes stand in a row like fence posts. Blue, pink, yellow and black fill every gap. It is drawn on June 8, 2022, four days after the first part of the series ends, and the whole room is already in it. Both eyes are cancelled. The mask summer begins with a face that has decided, before anyone looks at it, not to look back.
A pink mask with a red X in one eye, a ring in the other, a tongue hanging out at the bottom, and a column of brown beads down the right edge.
A pale mask with concentric rings for one eye and a red X for the other, a grid of white teeth, and a row of red flowers down the right.
A dark green head with a red X eye at the right, a row of white fangs, and a stack of blue bars at the lower left, framed in white.

Two square eyes side by side, each a tight spiral, the left orange and the right black and white, in a boxy head with a mouth of zigzag teeth below. Thick white and black lines run around the lower half in right angles, like the wiring of a machine. The ground is red and olive behind the head. It is the clearest statement of the room's formula: the eyes are boxes, the spirals are in the boxes, and everything else is pattern. Two spirals is a dazed face. It was drawn the day after the artist gave away 300 nifties to everyone who held an ink, and dazed is a fair reading of a summer in which the artist was drawing a mask a day and handing out the rest.
A yellow mask with a ringed planet for one eye, a red X for the other, a blue flower between them, and a mouth of white bars.
A grey round head with two yellow spiral eyes and a grin of yellow fangs sits between two figures in black, each with an X on its chest.

Late June to mid July. The box becomes a head with a jaw, teeth get bigger, and crowns of spikes stand up along the top. These are the weeks of the chic city cat club, when the artist was sending a free cat to every holder of an ink.

A purple ground, and in it a head with a yellow crown, two eyes that are each a mouth of fangs, and below them a wide grille of white teeth in a pink box. The face is drawn in black and white line over orange, blue and green scribble, and purple zigzag runs down the right side. It is the mask with the most teeth in the room: two sets in the eyes and one across the jaw. A crown over eyes that bite is the first crowned mask of the summer, from June 28. The crown comes back in September and October on nearly every head, and the thing it sits on never gets kinder than this.
A grey head with a crown of orange sun rays, two spiral eyes in yellow boxes, a row of boxes with X marks down the center and a mouth of white fangs at the bottom.
A mask with a flower for one eye and a red X in a spiral for the other, a mouth of yellow loops, and a small face in a box at the lower left.
A blue mask with a spiral in a box on the left and a ringed eye on the right, a bar of white teeth at the bottom, blue and pink scribble filling the face.
A black mask on red with a crown of orange bars, a yellow X in one eye, a ringed eye in the other, and a yellow fence of teeth at the bottom.
A red framed mask with two square eyes, one a spiral in orange and one a spiral in black, a row of white teeth at the lower left and bars of green and blue below.
An olive mask with a red ringed eye and a white ringed eye, a mouth of yellow fangs under a bar of blue, and a grille of white teeth at the bottom.

July 19 to August 19. The boxes turn into machines and mazes, and three of the last four masks are among the most worked drawings in the room. From August 16 each one was posted with its price, fifteen xDai, and from August 24 the price fell to five.
A red and black head with a crest of white and yellow stripes on top, a grille of blue teeth, and a second mouth of white bars at the bottom.
An olive machine of boxes with a pink spiral in a red box at the upper left, a smaller spiral beside it, and a thick black zigzag running across the middle.

A maze of boxes in red, yellow and blue, with a purple spiral in a dark box at the right, a red curl at the center and a mouth of white blocks at the lower right. Black zigzag runs across the top, pink zigzag runs along the bottom, and a flower sits at the lower left corner. The face has almost disappeared into the pattern; what is left is a spiral where an eye would be and a row of teeth where a mouth would be. It was drawn on August 10, the day before the artist announced that the inks would burn. A mask that has become a maze is a good picture of a mind deciding something.
A boxy head turned to the right, with a yellow loop of beads along its jaw, a square eye at the right, and a grille of teeth under a row of orange tiles.

A brown head with a yellow chain of beads around it, a pink box for one eye with a blue ring in it, a flower for the other, and a curling brown mustache over a long grille of white teeth. Three brown legs with white teeth hang below the mouth like a beard. Striped blue and yellow bars stand at the bottom like a collar. With 334 recorded strokes it is one of the two most worked masks in the room, and the only one with a mustache. It was made on August 12, the day after the burn announcement, and it is the funniest mask of the summer. Whatever the burning meant to the artist, the next morning's drawing was a dandy.
A mask with a crown of spikes and two spiral eyes in boxes, one yellow and one white, a row of ringed teeth below and bars of yellow and blue on both sides.

A long yellow face with two pale eyes and a mouth of white and black bars, behind a cage of thin yellow and white lines that cross the whole square. Stripes of pink, red and green stand behind the face, and a crown of white and yellow zigzag sits on its brow. Where the first mask of June packed its boxes to the edges, this one stands back and lets the lines fall over it. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022, and posted that day at fifteen xDai with the rest of the week's masks. The eyes are not spirals or crosses. They are eyes, pale and level, and after ten weeks of masks the face behind the cage is looking out.

In June, the first mask is packed to the edges with boxes, and its eyes are a red X and a purple cross. In August, the last is a long yellow face behind a cage of lines, with two pale eyes that are almost human. The parts never changed. The arrangement did, and so did the summer: the first mask was drawn in a month of giving things away, and the last in the week the artist began to burn.

The masks in this room are round, or turned sideways. A head drawn as a ring or an oval, with a border of dots or spikes, and the parts arranged inside it: hearts, flowers, spirals and crosses for eyes, and a mouth of teeth that sometimes takes the whole lower half. Twenty-one works, from June 8 to August 19, 2022. Where the square masks next door are machines, these are faces, and most of them are laughing.

Six of them come from a single day, July 9, when the round mask was found and tried six times in twelve hours. Each of the six has a different pair of eyes. One has a heart pierced by an arrow. One has a flower and a heart together. One has a spiral and a flower. One has an eye like a wheel. It is the clearest day in the record of how the artist worked: find a shape in the morning, and by midnight have exhausted it.

Watch the mouth. In the first mask it is a small open hole with teeth inside. By August it is a jaw of white teeth as wide as the face. On August 11 the artist posted that the inks were approaching four hundred and would be burned, called the year on the board an expedition that was largely complete, and drew a sun with a grin. Jamie Thingelstad bought it that night. The last mask in the room is a skull with one gold eye, drawn on the last day of the mask summer.
Before the round masks there were two oval ones, a week apart: a gold head with a spiral eye, and a grey skull with a grin.

A gold head in a frame of dark teal, drawn in loose loops of pink, blue and yellow line over a painted face. One eye is a spiral, the other is a cross in a box, and the mouth is a small open hole with teeth drawn inside it. Two red bars cross the brow. It is the first work of the mask summer, drawn on June 8, 2022, and it still has a painted face under the line, something the later masks let go of. Look at the mouth: a small hole, open, with the teeth inside and not bared. It is the mouth of someone about to say something. Ten weeks of masks follow, and none of them is this unguarded.
A grey skull in a grey room, drawn in white and black line with spiky blue lashes, a grin of white teeth and yellow and red bars behind it.
July 9, 2022. Six round masks in twelve hours, each with a different pair of eyes. The artist had announced the chic city cats two days earlier, and sat down to play.

A round mask on blue, with a red heart pierced by an arrow for one eye and a yellow flower for the other, a grille of white teeth in a box below, and a border of zigzag and beads around the edge. The face is filled with blue, red and green scribble, and a green coil sits at the lower left like an ear. It is the first of the six, and the arrow through the heart is the one thing in the room that tells a story. A heart with an arrow in it is the oldest sign for being in love, and this is a mask with that sign where its eye should be: a face that looks at everything through the thing it feels. The flower in the other eye agrees. It is the happiest mask in the wing, and it started a day of six.
Half an hour later, a round mask on teal with a red X in a white box for one eye and a black spiral in a red box for the other, a mouth of white fangs below.
A pale blue mask with a border of purple dots, a wheel for one eye, a ringed eye for the other, and a mouth of white bars at the lower right.
A round mask on blue with a red heart for one eye and a lilac flower for the other, a bar of white teeth crossing the lower face, and a border of yellow petals.

An olive mask with a big blue spiral for one eye and a small red flower for the other, a mouth of white fangs in a red box, and a border of yellow spikes with pink and blue beads. Where the morning's first mask had a heart and an arrow, this one has a spiral so large it fills a quarter of the face, and the flower beside it is pushed up into the corner. The eyes do not match in size, color or kind. The spiral is dizziness and the flower is pleasure, and the mouth under them is bared. Five masks into the day, the game has turned a little feverish.

A dark oval mask with a flower for one eye and a crossed eye for the other, a grille of white teeth, and a border of blue beads inside a ring of black spikes, on a ground of dark teal scribbled with yellow. The last of the six, twelve hours after the first, and the most worked, with 382 recorded strokes. The border is as busy as the face: beads, spikes, yellow loops and a second ring of blue around all of it. The day began with a heart and ends with a cross: the eye that was in love in the morning is cancelled by midnight, and the other has kept its flower. That is a day's work, and a fair portrait of one.

July 10 to 27. A beam returns, two hearts make a pair of eyes, a mask grows a beak, and the line loosens. On July 20 the artist burned an earlier series on another chain and called the Faces origin piece the last and only one of its kind.
A gold framed head with two glowing eyes, beams pouring from them across the square, a grille of grey teeth and a row of red bars at the bottom.
A yellow mask with two red hearts for eyes, a wide mouth of white teeth in a red box, and a black border drawn in one loose loop, the day after the six.
A magenta mask with a beak like a bird, a ringed eye at the left and a cluster of yellow dots at the right, a mouth of white and yellow bars, and a border of green beads.
A green and yellow mask with a black spiral at the upper left and a round eye with a red band across it, a mouth of red fangs and a second mouth of white teeth below.
A sketchy face on olive, drawn in black, yellow and orange loops, one dark eye at the left and a ringed eye at the right, a pink spiral on the cheek and a mouth of white teeth.

August 11 to 19. The mouth takes over. Six masks with jaws of white teeth as wide as the face, and a skull to end the room. The first of them was drawn on the day the burning was announced and bought by the collector within hours.

A round mask on dark blue with a crown of yellow rays, a white flower for one eye and a square with a spiral for the other, and a wide grin of white teeth curving across the lower half. Red zigzag runs down the left side of the grin, and small blue and yellow drops fall beside it. The rays around the edge are drawn as yellow spikes with white beads between them, so the head is a sun. It was drawn on August 11, 2022, the day the artist posted that the inks were approaching four hundred, that every one would gradually be burned, and that the year's expedition into the world of NFTs was largely complete. The same thread spoke of a journey into the sun and asked who still wanted to come along. Jamie Thingelstad bought this sun that evening, for fifteen xDai, and two days later bought the Faces origin piece for five hundred. The grin is wide and the drops beside it could be sweat or tears. The sun had been announced.
A big round head with a red target for one eye and a triangle with a blue eye for the other, a jaw of white teeth in a red mouth, drawn in black line over yellow and green.
A mask with a blue spiral eye and a red square eye, a flower at the right, a jaw of white teeth at the left, and a pale blue bar running down across the face like a strap.
A boxy head on red and blue with a green ringed eye and a red ringed eye, a long nose, and a row of white triangle teeth in a black mouth.

A brown round mask with a yellow eye and a green eye, blue bars for a nose, and a jaw of white teeth that takes up the whole lower half, with a yellow zigzag running along the bottom lip. Orange flames stand at the top corners. The head is drawn as one thick black ring over soft brown paint. In June the first mask had a small hole of a mouth with teeth drawn inside; here the mouth is the biggest thing on the face. It was drawn on August 17, with the burning under way and each day's masks posted at fifteen xDai. The flames at the corners are small. The grin is enormous. Whether the mask is laughing at the fire or because of it, the drawing does not say, and that is the summer.
A head in profile on red-brown, facing left, with a yellow eye in a box, a black zigzag along the brow, and a mouth of white bars at the lower left.

A grey skull with one eye a ring of teal and one a gold target with spikes, a red beam leaving the gold eye to the right, and a mouth of white and black bars. The skull is drawn in white and black line over grey and gold paint, with purple and blue scribble falling through it. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022, a few hours after the last square mask. The summer that began with a gold face about to speak ends with a grey skull with a beam coming out of its eye, still looking, still bared. The next day the series turned to cats.

The six masks from July 9 were made in one day, and every one of them has a different pair of eyes: a heart and a flower, an X and a spiral, a wheel and a ring. Then look at the brown mask from August, where the mouth has taken over. The eyes were the game in July. By August it was the jaw, and the jaw was grinning at a bonfire the artist had just announced.

Heads buried in line. In this room the face is drawn, and then drawn over, until it sits inside a tangle of colored scribble like a thing seen through weeds. Most of the grounds are black, slate or brown, and nearly every mouth shows its teeth. Twenty-eight works, from June 16 to August 19, 2022, and they are the darkest of the mask summer: the square and round masks next door are toys, and these are not.

Two things happen under the scribble. Some of the heads are painted first, with shadow on the cheek and light on the brow, and the line is laid over paint. Others are nothing but line, and the head is the place where the scribble gets densest. The difference is easy to see once you look for it: paint has edges that are soft, and line has none. In February the artist wrote that it is not the task of a work to fully reveal itself to the recipient, and called art a dope that makes every exploration unique. These heads are that sentence drawn: a face is there, and the line is what keeps it from being handed over.

The room's busiest stretch is one week, July 26 to 31, with fourteen heads in six days, in the middle of the month the artist was handing out cats to every holder and writing about an open-ended collection named after Warhol's Index Book. Watch the teeth across that week. They end up as the one clear thing in a face that has otherwise come apart, and then, on the last day of the summer, the scribble turns to soft gold rings and the face is only spirals.
June 16 to July 8. A profile on red, then a run of heads painted in gold and brown with the scribble drawn on top. The painted ones are the ones with feeling in them.
A black skull in profile inside a black square on red, drawn in a few yellow and white lines, with a spiral eye, a row of yellow teeth and a stitched line running down the back of the head.

A horned head painted in gold, brown and blue, with heavy lids and a bearded jaw, drawn over in pink, white and blue line. The paint underneath is modelled: the brow catches light, the cheeks fall into shadow, the beard is a block of dark strokes. The line on top loops around the horns and down the face without covering it. It is the first painted head in the room, made June 24, and the one where the paint and the line are most clearly two layers. The lids are heavy and the horns are small. This is a tired devil, and the scribble over it is not a disguise so much as weather.
A furry monster in the dark with two narrow eyes and a wide open mouth of white teeth, its fur a mass of green, red, blue and white scribble edged in white.
A brown head with a crown of spikes painted in gold, blue and purple, two round ringed eyes and a small zigzag mouth, framed by grey loops.

An elephant's head, or a skull with a trunk, painted in gold and purple with a red target for one eye and a pink spiral for the other, a mouth of white teeth at the bottom of the trunk. Yellow, blue and white scribble runs over the whole head, and purple drips fall from the jaw. The two eyes are the room's two kinds at once: a target on the left and a spiral on the right. It was drawn on July 4, 2022. One eye is aimed at and the other is dizzy, and the trunk ends in teeth. Of all the heads in the room it is the one most plainly in distress, and the drips from the jaw are the picture admitting it.
A dark round head in a frame, lit by two gold beams from the upper left, its open mouth a ring of white teeth, painted in brown and gold with scribble over it.
A green head with a grinning mouth of white teeth, two narrow eyes under a dark brow, and a crest of spikes, painted and scribbled on dark green.
Four heads from July 19 to 26. A red X returns to an eye, a brown head wears a bucket, and the line starts to take over. The cats were going out to every holder that week.
A dark head with a red X in one eye, a yellow bar across the brow like a headband, and a grille of white teeth, drawn in dense colored scribble.

A brown head on pale blue, painted in purple and tan with a flat top like a bucket, half-closed eyes and a grin of small teeth. Yellow and white dashes ring the head like a string of lights, and purple line loops around it. It is the one head in the room that smiles with its eyes closed, and the only one on a light ground. It was drawn on July 23, in the week the artist was sending a free cat to every holder of an ink and posting their names with thanks. A contented face, drawn once, in the middle of the summer's generosity, and then not again.
A head on purple, painted in brown and red, with one dark eye and one eye of white rings around a red center, a mouth of white teeth, drawn over in blue and white line.
A tangle of dark grey, white and pink line with a small red devil at the right, its spiral eye and grin of white teeth the only clear thing in the picture.

July 26 to 31, fourteen heads. The scribble is densest here, and the teeth are the one clear thing in most of them. In the same days the artist was naming the Index collection, a series that would only grow when every copy of the last piece had sold.

A face in black scribble on orange, with a red X over one eye and a white ring for the other, a yellow bar across the brow, and two rows of white teeth in a dark mouth. The black line is drawn thickest here of any work in the room, in heavy vertical strokes down the cheeks. The X is as big as the eye socket and drawn in red over the black. It is the angriest head in the room, and it was made on July 26, the first of fourteen in six days. The cancelled eye, the bared teeth and the black pouring down the face say one thing together, and the orange behind them says it loudly.
A head seen from the side on dark purple, its eye a blue spiral the size of a fist, its mouth a row of white teeth, drawn in orange, blue and black line.
A slate ground, a boxy head drawn in green, orange and white line, a red X over one eye, and a wide grin of white teeth in a red jaw.

A painted head on grey, in brown, black and gold, with two eyes that look out, a flat nose and a closed mouth, drawn over in yellow and purple line. Nothing is bared here. It is the one head in the room with its mouth shut and its eyes open, and the one most like a person. With 296 recorded strokes it is also the most worked. The eyes are level and a little sad. In a week of fourteen heads that grin and snarl through scribble, the artist stopped on July 28 to paint one that simply looks back, and then covered it with line as if to take it back. It is the nearest thing in the wing to a self-portrait, and nothing in the record says it is one.
A bear-like head on brown with two ringed eyes, a red mouth of white teeth at the bottom, and a second row of teeth above it, drawn in dense colored scribble.
A brown figure with a mop of hair, square glasses, a grin of white teeth, and a coat drawn in gold and brown strokes, sitting on a brown ground, the one in the week that is pleased with itself.
A slate ground, a mask with a spiral eye in a yellow box and a red arrow driving through its mouth of white teeth, drawn in pink, blue and yellow line.

A dark head with a spiral eye at the right and a red X at the left, white teeth in a red mouth, and the yellow bar again, in dense red, blue and white scribble, four days after the heavy black face on orange.
A black skull in profile on red and orange, facing right, with a yellow crown of spikes along the back of the head, a spiral eye, a mouth of white teeth and a yellow bar through the face.
One work from August 19, made the same day as the last masks and a week into the burning: a face of spirals in soft gold.

A face made of spirals: a square spiral for one eye, a round spiral for the other, a third spiral at the right edge like an ear, and a mouth of white zigzag. Everything is drawn in thin black and gold line over soft gold circles, and the whole square is a ring of rings. Where the first head in the room was a black skull in a box on red, this one has no edge at all. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022, with 57 strokes, a week after the artist began burning the unsold inks. Nothing in it is angry. The spirals go round and the gold is warm, and after ten weeks of teeth the summer ends on a face that is only dizzy, and at peace about it.

The first skull is flat black in its box on red. The last face is spirals in gold. The one is all edge and the other is all circle. In between, the scribble closed over the faces and the teeth were what was left showing. A head that will not reveal itself is still a head that wants to be looked at, and the artist spent the summer drawing twenty-eight of them.

Between June 8 and August 19, 2022, nearly every drawing was a mask. This room holds the twenty-one that were not. A figure with a balloon in a city, a man in a cage of red rain, a crow, a valley, a robot in the sun, a dog, a tree, a skeleton by a river. They were drawn in the gaps between the masks, sometimes on the same day, and they are what the artist drew when the mask came off.

They do not share a look. Some are a few lines on white. Some are painted. Some are as packed as the masks themselves, and two are crowds of masked figures standing together like a family photograph. What they share is that each one has a place in it: a street, a cage, a field, a fence, a sky. The masks have none; they fill the square. Nearly everything here stands on a line, or under a sky, or beside a wall, and the feeling of the room is the feeling of being somewhere.

Two of these were the cheapest works in the series: the skeleton in the CCO SUMMER shirt and the figure with a sun for a head, each bought by Jamie Thingelstad for a single xDai in the first week of August, the week the artist announced an open collection named after Warhol's Index Book and wrote that collectors should collect more of what they do not like, because the artist who is not what you are looking for today may open a whole world for you tomorrow. The tree with 1,758 strokes, the most worked drawing in the collection, was made on August 12, the day after the burning began.
Six works from June 14 to 28. A figure in a patterned field, a figure with a balloon, a figure in ink, a man in a cage, a crow, and a valley.
A red figure with spiral eyes and a grin stands in a field of yellow, green and purple pattern, a small black figure at its feet, white lines looping over everything.

A black figure with a red face and a red chest walks through a pale city holding a red balloon on a long string. The buildings are a few thin lines, a tower, a fence, a window grid, and the sky is patches of blue and pink. The balloon has a small crown drawn on it. Fifty-four recorded strokes make the whole scene, and the figure, drawn in solid black with a thin red edge, is the one dark thing in it. A figure alone in a city with a balloon is a picture of being small and holding on to one bright thing. The crown on the balloon is the joke: the thing it holds on to is royalty, and it is full of air.
A figure in black ink on white, seated with one leg out, its head a spiky skull with a grin, drawn in a few thick strokes and thin outlines.

A figure with a crown stands inside a cage of red lines on black, under a roof of yellow and white. The lines fall from the roof like rain, and the figure behind them is drawn in white and yellow line with spiral eyes and a grin, its hands drawn in white at the bottom. Forty-four strokes, nearly all of them the red bars of the cage. A crowned figure in a cage, grinning: the series keeps drawing kings, and keeps putting them behind bars. Six days earlier the figure with the balloon had its crown on the balloon. Here the crown is on the head and the head is locked up.
A crow with a red X eye and a red target on its wing stands on a perch in a storm of grey and black scribble, inside a grey frame.

A valley. A blue river runs down between yellow hills, a green ridge rises at the right, and a pale sky of white and blue clouds is drawn over with thin black lines. Everything is scribbled in loops, the hills in yellow, the ridge in green, the river in blue, but the loops follow the land. It is the one open landscape in the mask months, drawn June 28, 2022, the same day as the first crowned mask with fangs for eyes. On one day the artist drew the most threatening mask of June and this, a valley with a river in it and no one there. The two are the same hand, and the valley is the one it rested in.

July. A figure with a falling man, a maze of blocks, two crowds of masked figures, a robot in the sun, and a figure in the rain. These are the weeks the artist was handing out cats to every holder and writing that web3 had broken the barrier every artist had hoped the internet would break.
A painted figure in purple and gold with a spiral eye looks up at a small figure tumbling in the pink above, drawn in loops of yellow and blue line.
A maze of colored blocks in black, red, blue and green, with yellow beads running through it and a tiny white figure with raised arms at the bottom.

A dark crowd. Masked figures stand together in red, black and gold scribble: a skull with a crown at the left, a round head with a beam at the top, a face with a wide mouth of teeth at the right, and a small figure with a pale face at the bottom. A pink flower sits at the upper left. The figures overlap, and no one has the whole square. It is the first of two crowds in the room, drawn July 10, with 257 strokes, the day the artist wrote that web3 and NFTs had broken the barrier artists had hoped for since the internet began, the biggest change in any area of art in a long time. The crowd is what that sentence looks like from inside: everyone masked, everyone grinning, everyone in the same small space.

The second crowd, nine days later. Four masked figures stand in a row, each with blue ringed eyes and a red mouth of white teeth, a black cat with ex eyes beside them and a cat-eared figure at the upper left. The line is white and yellow over black and gold, and the figures are drawn more clearly than in the first crowd: each has a head, a body and a place in the row. Where the first crowd overlapped, this one lines up. The cat with ex eyes is from the spring. This is the block as a family photograph, and the family is wearing the masks from the rooms next door, the same red mouths, the same ringed eyes. Whoever they are, they have agreed to be seen this way together.
A gold robot with two red ringed eyes and a grille of teeth stands in rays of yellow sun, its body built from boxes, a flower at the upper left.
A figure in a gold hood stands in blue rain under a sun and a band of cloud, a yellow beam crossing it, its face a few dark marks in a glow.

July 31 to August 19. Two flat figures on one day, a skull in a summer shirt, a tree, and the last scenes of the mask months. The two cheapest purchases in the collection are here, and the most worked drawing.

A black dog stands on a black hill against pale blue, its mouth open, with short yellow wavy lines in a ring around it. Nothing is inside the black: no eye, no collar. It is the flat silhouette formula from the spring, drawn once more on July 31, 2022, in 49 strokes, in the middle of the mask months. A dog on a hill with its mouth open is barking or laughing, and the wavy lines say it is loud. After fourteen scribbled heads in six days, the artist drew this in a few minutes, and it is the clearest sound in the summer.

A figure with a sun for a head walks on black, its body a pink dress and its legs long yellow lines, with a ring of purple discs behind it like a flower; the collector bought it on August 2 for one xDai.

A yellow skull with blue goggles and a red cap, a grin of grey teeth, in a white tee that says CCO SUMMER, on black scattered with white marks, bought by the collector on August 8 for one xDai, as cheap as any ink he owns.

A tree in full leaf, painted in hundreds of small dabs of yellow, green, pink and red, standing behind a fence in a yellow light that falls from the upper left. The trunk is a few dark strokes under the mass of leaves, and the grass at the bottom is small dabs too. With 1,758 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the whole collection, and it is the one drawing in the mask months with no face in it at all. It was made on August 12, 2022, the morning after the artist announced that the inks would be burned and the first ink, the first thing ever sold, would be the last to go. The day after deciding to burn the year, the artist spent longer than on any other drawing putting leaves on a tree, one dab at a time. Nothing in the series says more plainly what the drawing was for.
A yellow figure with a long striped neck curls around itself in a field of orange, pink and blue bars, its head at the upper left with a grin of teeth.
A figure with long black hair over a blue body stands on brown, its face a yellow flower with two red ex eyes and a grin of white teeth, small flowers at its feet.
A purple skull with green hair and two red spiral eyes grins on slate, with blue rays around its head and yellow beads at its neck.

A dense scene by a river: two white skeletons stand on a black mound at the upper left, a pink pig with a crown sits at the lower right, a yellow sun with a spiral at the center, and a black bridge with a yellow stripe crosses the top right. Red and blue lines loop over the whole picture. It is the last work of the mask months, drawn August 19, 2022, and the only one in the room with a crowd, a creature, a sun and water all together. The skeletons from the winter, the crown from the summer, the sun from the burn announcement and a pig wearing the crown: on the last day of the masks the artist put the whole year on one riverbank and drew a bridge over it.

The figure with the balloon walks through a city drawn in a few lines. By the river, everything is packed in at once. Both are places. The masks of the summer have no place at all, and that is why these twenty-one hang together. The tree in the middle of them, a thousand dabs of leaf made the day after the artist began to burn the inks, is the quietest answer in the wing to the question of what all this was for.

Cats, and then creatures. For two weeks at the end of August 2022 nearly every drawing was a cat: black, boxy, big-eared, standing or sitting in a striped room with its teeth showing. Then, in the first days of September, the cats gave way to flat single creatures, each one color on one color. Twenty-six works, August 20 to September 14. The cats of the spring had been silhouettes with spiral eyes; these are built like the summer's masks, with bodies, and they have come indoors.

The cats are made from boxes, rings and grilles, but they have rooms to stand in. Stripes run behind them like wallpaper or a fence. Two of them share one drawing, and that drawing exists twice, published 85 seconds apart, the second time with a signature. They were drawn in the first fortnight of the burning: on August 23 the artist repeated that all four hundred inks would gradually be burned, and that everything after that was part of a new story. The next day the price of a new ink dropped from fifteen xDai to five, and Jamie Thingelstad bought the two cats drawn that day, the seated one in the red room and the white one in the yellow room.

Watch the stroke count fall. The cats are drawn in two to five hundred strokes. The flat creatures that follow them take thirty to fifty, and the room ends on a scribbled horse that takes forty. A series that had spent the summer burying faces in line spent September drawing one creature at a time in one color, as if the burning had made the drawing lighter.
August 20 to 24. Six cats in five days, from a crowned cat mask to a white cat on yellow. The day after the first of them, the artist minted a three-copy series on Ethereum called i was famous.

A black cat mask with a yellow crown sits on a dark red body, on a ground of gold scribbled with yellow bars. One eye is a blue ring with a cross in it, the other a yellow ring with a Z. The mouth is a box of white teeth under a yellow zigzag. It is the first work after the mask summer, drawn on August 20, 2022, and it is both things at once: the last mask and the first cat. The artist posted it that day at twenty xDai, five more than the masks around it. A crowned black cat with one eye cancelled is the summer's mask given a body and a name, and the price says the artist thought so too.
A black cat head with one red spiral eye and one blue, a grin of white teeth, and a crest of green, set in a weave of blue, yellow and black bars.
A cat figure stands with one arm raised in a room of purple and blue stripes, two round yellow eyes with flowers in them, a box of teeth below.

A black cat with two glowing yellow eyes and a wide grille of white teeth fills the square, its ears tall, its chest a black block over a red rug. The eyes are drawn as yellow rings with light inside them, and the teeth are a long bar with black between each one. Stripes of yellow, pink and white stand behind the cat like a curtain. With 395 recorded strokes it is the densest of the first cats. The glowing eyes are the May beams come back, and the grille of teeth is the summer's. This cat is sitting in the dark with the lights on, three days into the burning, and it does not look like it plans to leave.

August 24 to 26. A seated cat in a red room, a white creature in a yellow one, a cat on cream, and a drawing of two cats that was published twice. The first two were bought by the collector the day they were drawn, for five xDai each, the new price.

A black cat sits upright in a room of blue and red stripes, its face a white loop with a spiral eye, its body ruled with pink lines like a cage; bought by the collector the day it was drawn, August 24, for five xDai, a minute after the white cat.

A white cat with a long neck and a red mouth sits in a yellow room, a small black cat at its feet and a bird on a perch at the upper left; bought the same evening, also for five, the first of the two.

A black cat stands on a cream ground with a red X over each eye, its ears tipped in pink, a grin of white teeth, and a pink collar around its neck. Its tail rises in a hook. The room behind it is pale: a few blocks of orange, blue and grey, and thin lines running in loops. It is the quietest cat in the room, and the first with the X in both eyes. A cat with a collar is somebody's cat. The X in both eyes and the grin are the summer's, and the collar is new: of all the cats in the room this is the one that has a home, and it is the one that cannot see.

Two black cats side by side, the left one with a red X over one eye and a blue ring in the other, the right one with a red X and a green box. A small blue cat sits between them on a shelf. Below them a maze of black boxes with white line, and a yellow spiral at the right edge. The drawing was published on August 25, 2022, without a signature. Two cats and a small one between them is a family, and the maze under them is the block.

The same drawing, published again 85 seconds later, with one addition: the yellow signature at the lower right. Everything else is the same, the two cats, the small blue cat, the maze. Nine more strokes were recorded, and they are the signature. Both were kept, and both hang here, because the record kept both: on Nifty Ink a drawing is published the moment it is saved, and the artist, who signed nearly everything, had forgotten the signature and went back for it. It is the smallest story in the collection and one of the truest: a minute and a half, and a name.
A cat-eared mask with two ringed eyes full of green and pink line, a cage of white teeth in a red mouth, and yellow beads along the right edge, on pale blue.
August 26 to 28. Two cats drawn in white, a dense scene with a bird, a scribbled cat on cream, and a cat robot in the dark.

A white cat on black, its face a mass of pink, blue and yellow line, with a red X over one eye and a wide open eye on the other side, a blue beam coming in from the left, and a wide grin of white teeth. The ears are tall and striped. Blue and pink beads run down both sides. Its 437 recorded strokes are the most in the room. One eye cancelled and one eye wide open, with a beam hitting the face: it is the wing's whole argument in one cat. The grin is enormous and the open eye is terrified, and the drawing is honest enough to give both the same weight.
A dense scene with a yellow bird on a perch, a rocket, a creature in a green net, a figure with spiky hair at the lower left and a pink face at the right, on black with white crosses.
A black cat robot with a green box eye and a red box eye, a grille of white teeth, and a yellow zigzag running down its side, in the dark.

August 28 to September 2, and one horse from September 14. The drawings empty out. A white coat and a black figure on purple, a brown figure on maroon, and then single creatures in one color on one color. The two crowned creatures leaning on each other were bought by the collector on August 30.

Two figures on purple: a white coat with a red cap, drawn in a few black lines, and a small black figure with a cloud of curly hair and a yellow eye. Eighty-two recorded strokes. Two days after the white cat on black, with its hundreds of lines, the drawing has emptied out to two shapes and a flat ground. The white figure looks up and away; the small black one looks out. It is a picture of two people in a room not talking, and after a summer of masks it is the first drawing in the wing that is about two people.

Two creatures with crowns and red ringed eyes lean on each other on a floor of yellow stripes, in a room of blue stripes, drawn in white, pink and black line; the collector bought it on August 30, for five xDai.
A dark red figure dances on yellow, one leg raised, its head a long oval with a few yellow stitches, drawn in thirty-one strokes.
A blue creature with a crest of zigzag and a yellow spiral eye walks on dark red, one arm held out, its body striped with the ground color.
A pink creature with a crocodile snout, a target eye and a crest of spikes stands on black with one leg raised, its fur drawn in pink zigzag.
A teal creature drawn in line only, with a crest of zigzag, a red target eye and red teeth, standing on dark grey with its arms hanging.

A black skull in profile on lavender, with an X for an eye and a few purple lines for the jaw and the teeth, ringed with short black wavy lines. A black oval lies below it like a shadow. It is the flat silhouette from the spring, back for one drawing, and the X that sat on the cats' eyes is now the only mark on the face. In April the same formula made a bear hugging its belly. On September 2, with the inks burning, it made a skull, and the wavy lines that once made a cat hum now make a skull hum, which is a different sound.
Twelve days later, a horse drawn in yellow, orange and white scribble over a black body, walking on teal with its head down and a mane of white lines, the day before the Ethereum Merge.

Look again at the first cat, crowned and packed to the edges of the square, and then at the skull in profile, one black shape on lavender. The room moved from hundreds of strokes to a few dozen in two weeks, while the artist burned the year's inks and sold the new ones for five xDai. The X stayed in the eye the whole way. The cats, like the masks, never stopped grinning, and the grin never settled whether it was pleased or in pain.

Heads that look like people. After a summer of masks, the faces in this room have brows, lids, cheeks and worried eyes. They wear hats. Some are painted, some are a single line, and a few are skulls lit by colored beams. Twenty-three works from August 20 to October 5, 2022, the last seven weeks of the series. The masks hid someone. These show who.

The eyes do the work. A mask's eyes are rings and spirals; these eyes have whites, pupils and lids, and most of them look somewhere. An old man looks past you. A woman with pink hair looks down. A face in blue line looks straight out with tears on its cheeks. Five of the heads were drawn on September 15, 2022, the day Ethereum changed how it ran, the Merge the whole network had waited years for; two of them are skulls lit by beams, and none of them is celebrating.

Jamie Thingelstad was by now the series' most constant buyer. On September 28 he drew n n x y z fan art number zero zero zero 1 on the board, his block letters over the artist's scribble, and wrote that n n x y z was one of his favorite artists on Nifty Ink. He bought three of the heads in this room, one in September and two in the first days of October. Watch what happens on October 3, when three portraits are drawn in a morning with almost no color, in a single wandering line. After them the room closes with two round heads in goggles, each with words beside it, and the words are a motto: inkers gonna ink.

August 20 to September 2. A head in black scribble on red, an old man with worried eyes, and a face on yellow with a red target for one eye. These are the first faces after the mask summer, and the first that are frightened.
A head drawn in heavy black scribble on red, its face a tangle of pink line, a single yellow bar across the eyes like a blindfold.

An old man's face fills the square, painted in grey, green and yellow with scribble over it, his eyes wide and unmatched, his mouth open on a row of teeth. The brow is furrowed and the cheeks are hollow. Blocks of blue, green, yellow and red stand around him like a wall. It is the first face in the series that looks frightened, and with 267 recorded strokes one of the most worked in the room. It was drawn on August 29, 2022, in the third week of the burning, the same day as the sun with an X for an eye in the next room. The masks grinned through the whole summer. The first face without a mask is afraid, and it is afraid in the open, with its mouth hanging.
A head on yellow, painted in grey and green, with a red spiral target for one eye and a red cross for the other, its teeth bared, a striped collar below.

September 6 to 8. Figures lit by beams, a wrapped head in goggles, a man in a bucket hat, a profile in line, and a face under a top hat. The collector bought the wrapped head the day after it was drawn.
Two dark figures stand against black, each with two glowing yellow eyes, and beams of gold pour from the eyes down to the lower left.
A head wrapped in white bandages on yellow, with two round black goggles and a grin of pointed teeth, the mummy the collector bought the day after.

A man in a green bucket hat, painted in pink and brown, with two round glasses over two round eyes and a round open mouth. His neck is thin and his shoulders are lost in a town of blocks and lines in red, blue and black. The hat is drawn in green and black with the brim turned down. He is the first person in the series to wear a hat and glasses. Three round things on a face, two glasses and a mouth, all open: he is the picture of someone who has just been told something. It was drawn on September 8, 2022, the day the artist posted two more heads at five xDai and a week before the Merge.
A profile in line on dark green: a head with yellow hair, a pink face, one eye looking out, and a blue coat, drawn in thirty-seven strokes.
A red face under a black top hat, with two yellow crowns for eyes, a bar of white teeth and a row of yellow beads across the brow, on dark red.

September 14 to 22. A hatted face with fangs, a scribbled face with teeth, three skulls lit by beams, a gridded face and a woman with pink hair. Five of them were drawn on September 15, the day of the Ethereum Merge.
A face in a black hat with a spiral eye and a red eye, a mustache, a mouth of fangs, and green dots floating beside it, on a ground of blue stripes.
A painted face in grey and gold with a tangle of colored scribble over it, two round eyes, and a mouth of white teeth in a red frame.

A skull on lavender, painted in purple, green and pink, with a beam of color crossing its eyes from the left, and a row of white teeth at the bottom. One eye socket is filled with grey and red rings; the other is dark. Thin yellow and blue lines wander over the ground. The skull is the one in the room that is almost a face, with a nose and lips drawn in, and the color is the softest. It was drawn on September 15, 2022, the day of the Ethereum Merge, when the network the artist had bridged inks to for a year stopped mining and began staking. Five works were drawn that day, and this is the gentlest: a skull in candy colors with a rainbow across its eyes, as if a death's head could be a party.
A skull in grey, green and purple on a ground of soft olive circles, its eyes two dark hollows, a rainbow beam crossing from the left, the second skull of the Merge day.
A face in black and orange line on tan, its brow ruled like a grid, two round grey eyes, and a mouth of white bars.
A woman with pink hair looks down on tan, her face orange, her eyes two blue rings, her mouth a row of white marks, in a blue coat, the one person on the Merge day who is not looking at anything.

A skull in the dark, painted in black and grey with yellow and red line, two beams coming in from the sides to meet at the eyes, a row of white teeth below. Where the lavender skull was soft and lit from one side, this one is lit from both, and the light is the only color. Black fingers reach up from the bottom edge. The last of the five from the Merge day, and the darkest. A skull with two searchlights on it and hands reaching up from below is the series' picture of being looked at, and on the day the whole network was watching one event, the artist drew a skull in the crossfire.
A hatted face with a spiral eye, a mouth of white bars and a beam from the left, in a field of colored rays, drawn in yellow and black line; the collector bought it on October 3, for five xDai.
A cat-eared face in purple, pink and green with one huge eye and one small, a mouth of fangs, on dark navy.

A face under a black top hat, split into a dark red side and a yellow side, with two eyes of different sizes, a grin of white teeth, and two white-gloved hands below, the last head before the collector drew his fan art.

October 3 to 5, 2022. Three portraits in a single line, drawn in three hours, then two round heads in goggles to close the room. The collector bought the hatted face lit by a beam on October 3, and the first of the goggled heads the day after it was drawn.

A face on blue drawn in one black line, with tan patches for the cheeks, two eyes with white tears, a red mouth, and yellow zigzag for the hair. A hand rises at the left. The line wanders from the brow down the nose to the chin without lifting, and the color is laid on in a few flat patches. It is the first of three portraits drawn that morning, October 3, 2022, after eleven days away from the board. The eyes have tears in them, and the hand at the left is raised as if to say stop, or wait. After a year of grins the series' last portraits are of someone crying, and they are drawn more tenderly than anything before them.
A face on yellow drawn in black and red line, a tear on each cheek, red lips, the hair a loop of orange and black, drawn an hour and twenty minutes later, and also crying.
A face on olive drawn in yellow, black and red line, a red mouth the only solid mark, drawn in twenty-seven strokes an hour after the second, the sparest of the three.

A round yellow head on black with pink spots on its scalp, blue goggles, a mouth of white bars, and the words GRIFTERS GONNA GRIFT and INKERS GONNA INK written in blue beside it; the collector bought it the next day, for five xDai.

A round blue head on black with yellow spikes standing up from its scalp, pink goggles, and a sunburst for a mouth, with INKERS GONNA INK at the lower left.
