The day after the yellow head, the same shape returns in the opposite colors, with a beam of gold falling from the mouth. It is the last portrait in the series, drawn October 5, 2022. The words are the artist's: the year had been full of grifters, on the chains, in the marketplaces the artist spent the spring complaining about, and the answer was a head in goggles with light coming out of its mouth and a motto. Inkers gonna ink. Ten days later the series ended.

Look again at the old man from August, painted in a hundred small strokes with his eyes wide, and then at the face from October 3 drawn in one line with a tear on each cheek. The second has a tenth of the strokes. Both are faces that look at something, and that is what sets this room apart from the masks. The series ends its portraits with a head in goggles and a slogan, and the slogan is the artist's answer to what the year had been: grifters gonna grift, inkers gonna ink.

The last masks. Crowned, packed, and drawn in the dense scribble of the summer, these are the faces that ran alongside the cats and the portraits from August 20 to September 17, 2022. Then, after four weeks of silence, three works on October 15 close the series: the first drawing redrawn, which its title calls a fork; number 300; and the collection piece, number zero zero zero zero. Twenty-one works.

A crown is a zigzag of three or five points on top of the head. It sits on a mask with ex eyes, on a profile with a cigarette, on a winged figure, and on the skull of number zero zero zero zero. The three-pointed crown is the mark Jean-Michel Basquiat put on his heads forty years earlier, and the comparison is the gallery's, not the artist's: the artist never named him. But a crown on a skull with its eyes crossed out, drawn fast in scribble over flat color, is a thing Basquiat did, and here it is again on a drawing board on a side chain, drawn by someone who signed nearly every work with a scrawled tag: the year, two N's and xyz.

The series ended on a Saturday and changed hands on a Sunday. On October 15 the artist drew the three last works, and on the morning of October 16, 2022, Jamie Thingelstad bought number zero zero zero zero for 750 xDai, the highest price any ink in the series had carried. That afternoon, over four hours, the artist sent him the rest: 275 drawings, nearly everything from New Nifty on the Block that was not already in his wallet. The whole wing you have walked through arrived in one afternoon. Watch the first of the three October works: it is the first drawing in the series, drawn again ten months later, and the room's last word on what changed.
Four masks from the first day of the room, August 20, 2022, all crowned or spiked, drawn alongside the first cats in the first fortnight of the burning.
A dense face with two spiral eyes in boxes, a long nose and a small mouth, drawn in red, blue and orange line over stripes of every color.

A purple crown with a yellow zigzag sits on a grey mask whose right eye is a red X over a yellow ring and whose left is a box of bars. The mouth is a grille of white teeth in a red box. The body below is a cage of black and yellow lines on a red block, and green and purple bars stand at the edges. It is the clearest crown in the room, drawn on the first morning, August 20, 2022, with the burning nine days old. A crown over a cancelled eye and a grille of teeth: a king who cannot see and will not stop grinning. It is the summer's mask with the one thing added that turns it into a statement.
A mask in profile facing left, with a crown of black spikes, a yellow spiral eye and a long grille of white teeth, on orange scribbled with blue.
A dense mask with a red X in a round eye and a white ring for the other, a bar of blue across the brow, a mouth of white and black bars, on stripes of orange, blue and purple.
August 22 to 29. A crowned orange mask, a robot in white, a yellow face with a nose, and a sun with an X for an eye, drawn the same day as the frightened old man next door.
An orange mask with a crest of red spikes, a black spiral eye at the left, a white box eye at the right, and a mouth of white bars, on a ground of yellow and black bars.

A robot figure on white, its head a box with two glowing yellow eyes under spiky lids, a wide red mouth of white teeth, and a body of black and white bars with pink and blue inside. Red paint runs down the sides like spilled ink. It is the one mask in the room with a whole body and a white ground, and with the red at the edges it looks like it is standing in something. It was drawn on August 26 and posted at five xDai, the new price after the burn. A robot with lit eyes standing in a red puddle on a white page is the series' most cheerful drawing of a disaster.
A yellow face with a long nose, one eye a ring and the other a spiral, a bar of red across it, and a mouth of white teeth, on green and yellow bars.

A yellow sun with a face on a red ground: one eye an orange X, the other a black box, a zigzag of white teeth for a mouth, and pale drips running down from the bottom of the sun. Red strokes cross the sun from the left, and two small triangles stand at the bottom like tents. The sun fills most of the square and sits inside a soft white ring, so it glows. On August 11 the artist had written of a journey into the sun and asked who still wanted to come along. Eighteen days later, here is the sun: one eye crossed out, teeth bared, dripping. It was drawn the same day as the frightened old man in the next room. The destination and the traveller, on one Monday.

September 4 to 17. Eight masks: dense ones with ex eyes and teeth, a sparse robot on lavender, a profile with a cigarette, a white oval on black, a winged figure, and a profile lit by a beam. The last of them was the collector's purchase on October 5, with the series ten days from its end.
A dense mask with a red X in each boxed eye, a crown of yellow bars on top, a mouth of white teeth in a red box, and yellow ovals all around.
A purple scribble mask with a yellow bar through one eye and a blue cross over the other, two mouths of white teeth, and yellow drips from the top.
A mask with a crown of white spikes, a white ring eye and a red X eye, a mouth of white teeth in a red box, on brown with orange bars.

A robot mask on lavender drawn in a few lines, a red X in a black ring for one eye, a red bar for the other, a box of white and red bars for a mouth, and thin legs below it like a stand. Forty-one recorded strokes. Set beside the purple crowned mask from August, it is the same arrangement with the scribble taken out: the X, the box and the grille, and nothing else. It was drawn on September 6 and posted at five xDai. After a year of packing every square to the edge, the artist drew the mask in forty strokes and stopped, and it holds. The formula had become a signature that could be written fast.
A blue mask with two crowned eyes, one a ring and one a box, a wide mouth of white teeth in a red frame, and bars of red and orange at the sides.

A profile in pink line on slate, facing right, with a red spiral eye at the left, a cross in a ring at the right, a mouth of white teeth, and a cigarette drawn in white line with smoke at its tip. Blue hair in zigzag runs along the top. Fifty-four strokes. It is the one mask in the room that smokes, and the only one that looks relaxed about anything. A week before the Merge, the series drew a head in profile, in a few lines, taking a drag.
A dense mask with a red target eye and a dark eye, a mouth of yellow teeth in a pink box, a flower at the lower right, on orange and red bars.
A white oval mask on black, filled with fine colored scribble, with two ringed eyes, a dark nose, a small mouth and a red ear at the right.
A winged figure with a yellow head and two red ex eyes spreads black wings over a ground of brown, yellow and purple, a yellow bar across the bottom, the day before the Merge.

A profile in brown with a beam coming in from the left to a ringed eye, a grille of white teeth, and green and pink line over the face, on brown; the collector bought it on October 5, 2022, for five xDai, eleven days before he bought the whole series.
Four weeks after the last mask, three works on one day close the series, and the next morning the collector bought the last of them and received the rest.

The first drawing in the series, drawn again. A crowd of heads and raised limbs on cyan, with teeth at every size and a hand with spread fingers, as in December 2021. The colors are the same. The lines are looser and the figures larger, with a pink face at the center and a dark figure at the upper right. A small round badge sits at the lower left, and the title says fork. It was drawn on October 15, 2022, the first of the three that day. The word fork is the one a blockchain uses when a chain splits and goes on in two versions. The artist, who began the year with this crowd, drew it again at the end and called it a fork: the same block, a second time, and the people on it drawn bigger and looser by a hand that had made three hundred drawings since. The original is in the first room of this wing. The two are the series' beginning and its ending, and they are the same picture.

A skull mask in the dark with a glowing yellow eye and a beam coming in from the left, its mouth a grille of white teeth, blue bars along the top like a crown, and coils of green and purple at the sides. Number three hundred, drawn two hours after the fork. The light is the summer's light, from the beam room in May, falling on the summer's mask. Three hundred drawings in three hundred and eleven days, and the three-hundredth is a skull with one eye lit, which is the series looking back at itself: dead, crowned, and still watching.

The collection piece, an edition of one, drawn last on October 15, 2022, four hours after the fork. A purple skull in profile with a red X for an eye and a row of white teeth, under a crown of orange and red bars, with a yellow sun grinning at the upper right. Green bars stand at the left and yellow ones at the right. Everything the series drew is in it: the crown, the X, the grille, the sun, the beads, the scribble. Nothing else in the room took as many strokes: 448. The artist held it back from the board's usual pricing, as with the Faces in August, and put it up as the key to the series. On the morning of Sunday, October 16, Jamie Thingelstad bought it for 750 xDai, and that afternoon the artist sent 275 drawings to his wallet, one transfer at a time, from half past twelve until nearly five o'clock in Minneapolis. The skull under the crown with the sun grinning over it is the series' last self-portrait, and the day after it was drawn it became the deed to the whole block.

The fork of the first drawing and number zero zero zero zero hang side by side at the end. One is the series' first idea, redrawn. The other is everything the series learned in ten months, packed into a single skull with a crown on it and the sun grinning in the corner. Between them is the whole of New Nifty on the Block, and the morning after they were drawn, the whole of it went to one collector who had been buying it a drawing at a time since May.

People, painted fast. The Rawblocks series opens with a run of portraits, most of them drawn between November 5 and 9, 2022: a man in a plaid shirt with a cigarette, a hunched man in a cap, a figure in a hooded cloak of polka dots, a man in a beanie and beard. They are painted in soft discs of color with a loose line drawn over them, and the line is what makes them people. They are the most human pictures n n x y z made, and they were made in the week the crypto world's largest exchange collapsed.

Each one wears something. A cap, a bandana, sunglasses, a fur coat, a hoodie. The clothes are often more worked than the face, and the face is a few strokes: two eyes, a red mouth, a cigarette. The grounds are flat and plain, grey, olive, blue, so the figure is all there is. Nobody here is grinning. After a year of masks, the artist sat down on a Saturday evening in November and painted six people in two hours, and they look like people who have been up too late and heard bad news.

FTX began to fail on November 6, 2022, and filed for bankruptcy on the 11th. The artist posted once that week, on the 10th, that it was always funny to read that marketplaces think they have a choice and artists think they don't. The room opens with three cartoon heads from the first night and closes with two painted figures from January 2023, drawn after two months away. Watch how the painting changes between them, from a round yellow head to a woman in yellow light with no face at all.

October 30 and 31, 2022. Three cartoon heads to begin: a round yellow head in pink glasses, a face in sunglasses in orange rays, and a red-haired head on legs. Two weeks after handing the whole of New Nifty on the Block to the collector, the artist started again.

A round yellow head wearing pink glasses, with a small red mouth and one curl of hair, on a body in a blue coat holding out a black glove. The ground is teal with soft discs, and a row of yellow triangles stands on the head like a crown of spikes. It is the first Rawblocks work after the two masks of May, drawn October 30, 2022, and it is a cartoon: a circle for a head, a dot for a nose. It is also a sun with a face, the figure that ended New Nifty on the Block two weeks earlier, now wearing glasses and offering a hand. The new series begins where the old one stopped, and in a better mood.
A face in dark sunglasses drawn in yellow and purple line over a ground of orange rays, its mouth open on a row of white teeth.
A red-haired head on two black legs walks across orange, grinning with white fangs, one arm out, its hair a cloud of red scribble.
November 5, 2022. Six portraits in two hours, from a man in plaid to a hunched man in a cap. The next day the run on FTX began.

A man with a red cap of hair and blue eyes stands in a plaid shirt, painted in grey, brown and teal with white line over it, a cigarette at his lips. The ground is brown with dark shapes at the right. The shirt is drawn as a grid of lines over dark paint, and the face is a few strokes: two blue eyes, a red mouth, a line for the nose. The November portraits begin here, on the evening of Saturday, November 5, 2022. He is not a mask and not a cartoon. He is a man smoking, looking slightly to one side, drawn by someone who had spent a year not drawing people. The day after, the exchange began to fail, and the artist kept painting faces like this one through the week.
A man in a blue striped shirt sits with his hands on his knees, his trousers black with white stripes, on a grey ground, his small face painted in brown, waiting for something.
A man in a camouflage shirt raises one arm against dark green, his hair blue, his mouth red, drawn in white line over painted tan and brown.

A figure in a hooded cloak of blue and white stripes with yellow polka dots, a brown face inside the hood drawn in orange scribble with one blue eye, on teal inside a loose white frame. The cloak is painted in soft blue with the stripes and dots drawn over it. The face is small and the cloak is huge, and the frame around the whole thing is drawn in a few white strokes, like a window. Someone wrapped up against weather, seen through a window: it is the tenderest of the November figures, and the one most clearly drawn from feeling, with the formula set aside. The hood is the year's mask, turned soft.
A hunched man in a dark cap looks down against purple, his face painted in gold and brown with a red eye, a band of pink light crossing behind him, the last of the six that evening, and the saddest.

November 6 to 8, 2022. Eight portraits: glasses and curly hair, pink sunglasses, a cap and a cigarette, a bandana, a beanie and a beard. These are the days the exchange was failing, and the faces are the calmest the artist ever painted.
A man with curly hair and glasses in profile on olive, painted in grey and lilac, with red lips and a dark coat, the glasses drawn as a single lens, on the day the run on the exchange began.
A face drawn in black line with curly hair, lit by rainbow rays from behind, its eyes yellow and its mouth a grin of teeth.

A man in pink sunglasses and a blue hood, painted in brown and grey, his hair a crest of red and orange strokes, his mouth open on orange teeth with red drips falling from it. The sunglasses are one pink shape across the face with a dark lens. The hood is blue with white line. With 585 recorded strokes it is one of the most worked drawings in the room, and the drips are the one violent mark in a room of calm faces. Drawn on November 6, 2022. The man is dressed for a party and something is coming out of his mouth, and the sunglasses mean nobody can see what he thinks about it.

A man in a blue cap and sunglasses with a red beard smokes a cigarette, in profile on olive with a field of white dots behind him. The cap is drawn in blue with a dark brim, the sunglasses are black with a purple lens, and the beard is orange scribble. His jacket is red with white sleeves. The cigarette is drawn in white with a red tip. It is the room's most complete figure: hat, glasses, beard, jacket, cigarette, all in one. He is also the most composed. On a day when the people who held money on the exchange were trying to get it out, the artist painted a man taking a drag with his eyes hidden and his beard neat, and gave him a field of polka dots to stand in.

A profile in a red bandana and glasses, with a gold earring drawn as a spiral, red lips, and a yellow jacket, on a ground of soft yellow and pink discs. The bandana is drawn in red scribble with a blue band across it. The face is painted in pink and lilac and drawn over in black. At 708 recorded strokes, no other work in the room took as much drawing. The earring is the spiral that was an eye all year, moved to the ear, and the red lips are shut. This is the one portrait in the room that looks like it was made from affection for the person in it, whoever they were.
A painted head with green curly hair and a small red mouth on blue, its face grey and purple with two round eyes, a hand at the shoulder, drawn on November 8, the day the exchange stopped paying out.
The same head, half an hour later, with red goggles and a beam of gold pouring from its mouth to the right.

A man in a red beanie with a brown beard and blue eyes, in a yellow jacket, on blue. The face is painted in dark blue and brown with colored scribble over it, and the eyes are two rings under drawn lashes. The beanie is red with a folded brim. The jacket is yellow with a row of buttons. It is the last of the November portraits, drawn November 8, with 592 recorded strokes. The eyes are ringed like the masks' eyes but they have lashes, and they are looking straight out, worried. He is the one man in the room who meets your eye, and he was drawn the night the exchange halted withdrawals.
November 9, 2022, three cartoon heads with horns and goggles. Then, after ten weeks, two painted figures from January 23, 2023, from the week the artist came back to the board.
A cartoon head on red with pink lashes, yellow eyes, pink cheeks, a mustache and a horn, two black hands raised at the sides.
A dark cartoon head on purple with a crown of red dots and white spikes, orange lashes, and a beam of orange light crossing from the left, on a thin neck of bones.

A head with curly yellow hair, blue goggles, a red clown nose and white lips, on red, with green dots on the cheeks and a striped wand at the right, the clown drawn on the day the deal to save the exchange fell through.

A woman with dark hair in yellow light, her face a cloud of pale discs with no features but a blue mark and a small red mouth, her hands drawn in black at the lower corners. Sixty-eight strokes. Ten weeks after the man in plaid, the painting has gone soft: the light is the subject, and the face is almost gone. It was drawn on January 23, 2023, in the week the artist returned to the board after two months of silence. The collector had bought the dark head drawn five days earlier to celebrate the return. This is what the return looked like when it was quiet: a person in light, barely there, and the hands at the corners the only solid things.
A figure with purple hair looks up on black, its face painted in gold and green with scribble over it, one arm raised and the other reaching out, drawn in brown line, the last person in the series.

The man in plaid with his cigarette was drawn in a few strokes on the first evening of November, with the exchange that held half the market's money three days from going under. The woman in yellow light came in January, when the artist came back. Both are people. One is drawn in line over paint. The other is paint with almost no line, and the face has dissolved into the light. Between them the masks of the year were set down, and this room is what the artist drew without them.

Patterned masks, and then black figures. This room holds two things that look nothing alike and were drawn in the same two weeks of November 2022. First the masks: faces packed with pattern, hearts, hatching, spirals, crowns, drawn over paint until the square is full. Then the figures: flat black shapes on a bright ground, a girl in a dress, a creature on all fours, a man in the rain. The masks are the old vocabulary. The figures are something the series had not done before, and they came in the two days the exchange went under.

The two earliest works in the room are the two earliest in the whole series, from May 8 and 9, 2022, the weekend the Terra stablecoin began to fall, and they are masks too, packed to the frame. Jamie Thingelstad bought the first of them the day it was posted, his first Rawblocks, six months before the series properly began. The masks that follow in November turn into skulls and sun-faces, and then on November 10 the black figures arrive, three in one evening.

Watch the black. In the masks it is one color among many. In the figures it is the whole body, and everything else, the maze, the sun, the rain, is drawn around it. The girl with the flower was drawn on the evening of November 10. The man in the rain with the question marks was drawn on the morning of November 11, 2022, hours before FTX filed for bankruptcy. Nothing in the record says the artist drew the news. The drawings say what the week felt like.

May 8 and 9, 2022. The first two Rawblocks works, drawn six months before the rest: two dense masks inside white frames, made the weekend Terra began to fall. The collector bought the first the day it appeared.

A mask packed with pattern inside a white frame: a ringed eye in a box at the left, a spiral eye in a box at the right, a mouth of white bars, and around them columns of beads, zigzags and hatching in red, yellow, blue and green. Nothing is empty. The first Rawblocks work, drawn May 8, 2022, with 387 recorded strokes, the most in the room. It was drawn on the Sunday the Terra stablecoin began to slip, between the beam heads of the other series, and the next day Jamie Thingelstad bought it for twenty xDai: the first Rawblocks anyone owned, bought on the day the market broke. The name of the series means what it says. A raw block is a square filled until it is solid.
A second mask in a white frame, the next day, with a red target eye in a box, a gold eye in a leaf shape, and a wide mouth of white and red zigzag.

October 30 to November 9, 2022. Ten masks: a crowned face with a red X eye, a green skull, two pink faces with one eye each, a half-sun skull, a skull in red rays, and three on pink. The last six were drawn on November 9, the day the rescue of the exchange fell through.
A mask with a crown of red spikes, a red X over one eye and a cross over the other, a snarl of white teeth, on stripes of yellow and teal, the crowned skull of October brought into the new series.
A round green skull with two ringed eyes, one red and one blue, a crown of purple capsules, and a wide grin of white teeth, drawn over olive.

A face in profile on pink with one huge eye ringed in yellow and pink lashes, a red pupil, blue tubes hanging under it, and a small red mouth. The face is painted in dark red and drawn over in white and pink. A black shadow lies along the bottom. It is the first of a pair: the same face returns an hour later with blue hair. One eye, enormous, with the lashes drawn one by one, and a mouth too small to speak with: it is a face that is all looking, drawn on November 7, in the middle of the week everyone was watching one thing.
The same face an hour later, now with a crest of blue hair, a yellow flower in its mouth, and a yellow coat, on the same pink, and the flower makes it a joke.

A skull split down the middle: the left half painted in soft yellow with a pale eye, the right half a gold sun-face with a spiral eye and a ring of yellow rays. A rope of gold runs down between them. The mouth is a grille of white teeth in a gold box. The ground is a haze of orange and purple discs. Two faces in one skull, one quiet and one burning. It was drawn on November 9, 2022, the day the deal to rescue the exchange collapsed. The quiet half and the burning half share a jaw, and the grin is the same on both sides. It is the wing's thesis in one head: the calm and the panic are one face.

A skull mask in a field of red rays, drawn in white and blue line with a target eye crossed in red at the left and a spiral eye at the right, a grille of white teeth, and a crown of spikes. Bones cross below the jaw. The rays are short red strokes on dark grey, standing out from the skull on every side. Its 576 recorded strokes are the most of any mask in the room. A crowned skull with crossbones in a halo of red: the pirate flag and the saint's halo at once, drawn on November 9. The spiral eye is dizzy and the crossed eye is shut, and the rays say the thing is radiating something. On that day, it was probably not calm.
A patterned mask on pink, drawn in loose loops of white, green, blue and yellow, with two ringed eyes and a mouth of white bars.
A mask on pink with a red crown on a yellow head, a red spiral eye, a wheel eye, a rainbow mouth, and a ring of beads around the face.
A round mask with a crest of orange spikes and a spiral eye stands on a stick body with two blue arms, on brown.

November 10 and 11, 2022. A dark scribbled head, then nine flat black figures in two days: a girl, a creature in a maze, a tube figure, a ghost in a frame, a man in the rain. The exchange filed for bankruptcy on the 11th.
A dark head on navy with cat ears, two red-rimmed eyes and a mouth of white teeth, drawn in colored scribble over black, the last scribbled head before the black figures.
A black figure with spiky hair and yellow legs bends over in a tangle of yellow, white and pink pipes on pink.

A black figure on all fours in a maze of yellow pipes on green, its spiky head a ball with a red X eye and a grin, and three small black figures standing on its back. The big figure is one flat black shape with round feet. The maze is drawn in thick yellow strokes that fill every gap. The flat black figures begin here, and the small ones on its back are drawn the same way at a tenth of the size. A creature on all fours in a maze, carrying three others, drawn on November 10, 2022: the picture does not need the date to be a picture of being lost and carrying people, but it has the date.

A girl in a black dress with a white face and a ponytail stands in a teal frame, her hands white, a small red flower at her feet. The face is a white circle with two black eyes and an O mouth. The dress has a row of white buttons. Fifty-four strokes. A grey shadow falls behind her. It is the quietest figure in the room, and the only one with a flower. Her mouth is an O: she is surprised, or singing, or about to cry. She was drawn on the evening of November 10, 2022, with the exchange a day from bankruptcy and the artist posting that artists, unlike marketplaces, think they have no choice. A girl with a flower at her feet is the gentlest thing in the series, and it comes from the worst week.
A black creature with yellow bands on its arms raises both hands in a teal frame, two white eyes with blue pupils, a grin, and a small black figure standing on its head.

A black head in profile with spiky hair on olive, one white eye, and a white hand raised to its chin, inside a dark frame. Twenty-five strokes. The head is one black shape with a long shadow behind it, and the hand is white so it shows. It is the sparest work in the series, drawn on November 11, 2022, the day FTX filed for bankruptcy. The whole drawing is a person thinking. After a year of three hundred grins, the artist drew a head with its hand at its chin and no mouth at all, in twenty-five strokes, and it says more than most of the masks.

A patterned mask on pink with goggles, two ringed eyes inside them, a crown of white spikes, and a mouth of white teeth, drawn in yellow and black line, the mask coming back for a moment between the figures.

A black figure with a smiling X-eyed face and a red heart on its chest stands in blue rain under a yellow sun with a face, its arms out, two black hands rising at the bottom corners. Question marks float in clouds at the sides. It is drawn inside a cream frame. Where the girl in the teal frame stood still, this figure stands in weather, and the sun looks down at it with its own face. It was drawn on the morning of November 11, 2022, hours before the bankruptcy filing. The eyes are crossed out and the mouth is smiling and the heart is showing, and the clouds on either side say the one thing the whole week was saying: question mark, exclamation mark. It is the only drawing in the series with punctuation in it, and it needed it.

Six months separate the first mask, packed to its frame with beads and bars, from the black head in profile with its white hand, drawn in twenty-five strokes. The whole range of the series is between them: everything, and almost nothing. The first was drawn the weekend one stablecoin collapsed, the second the day an exchange did, and the artist's answer to the second was a black figure thinking, with its hand at its chin.

Heads in a few lines, then heads in a storm of them. This room begins in November 2022 with faces drawn in loose colored line on bright grounds, yellow, orange, magenta, green, and ends in March 2023 with the collection piece. Between them the winter heads arrive: dark, scribbled, with teeth bared. The series went quiet for two months after November 23, and when it came back in January the heads had gone black.

The line heads are quick. A black loop for the skull, a few colored strokes for the features, the ground doing the rest. The scribbled heads are the opposite: hundreds of strokes piled on a dark face until only the eyes and the teeth show through. When the first of them appeared on January 18, 2023, Jamie Thingelstad bought it that night and wrote that he was excited to see n n x y z, one of his favorite artists, publishing again after a couple of months away, and had bought it to celebrate. It is the dark head with two mouths.

The ground goes dark. It is yellow on November 16. By January it is black, and by February the faces have no ground at all, only scribble. In February the artist began posting that unsold editions would burn in the next days, and in March nearly sixteen hundred copies were minted straight into a burn address. The collection piece was drawn on March 15, 2023, and that evening the collector bought it for 300 xDai and received the sixty-three Rawblocks within three hours. The two landscapes painted after it hang in the coda next door.
November 16 and 17, 2022. Four heads in loose line on bright grounds, each drawn in under a day of the last, in the week after the exchange went under. The ground is still bright.

A head on yellow drawn in black line, with a red box around the face, one small eye at the left and one white ring at the right, and a grin of white teeth. Grey scribble fills the ground behind it, and a few blue lines run through the face. Sixty-two strokes. The head is a box inside a box, the way the masks were, but drawn in air: nothing is filled, and the yellow comes through everywhere. It was drawn on November 16, 2022, five days after the bankruptcy, and it is the lightest head in the wing, as if the artist had put the paint down and was drawing to see what was left. What was left was the box, the ring, the grin, and a lot of yellow.
A head in profile on orange, drawn in black line with a blue X for an eye, a grin of white and black teeth, and an ear drawn as a spiral.
A head on magenta in black and colored line, two ringed eyes, a crest of black scribble for hair, and a mouth of white teeth in a red box.
A head in profile on green, drawn in a single pink and yellow line, with a red eye and a mouth of white teeth at the right.
November 22 and 23, 2022. Three heads where the scribble comes in: a purple head with yellow hair, an orange cat head, and a head lit by a beam. Then two months of silence.
A purple head with a crest of yellow strokes for hair, two ringed eyes, and a wide grin of white teeth, in colored scribble on purple.

A cat head on orange, drawn in thick black loops over teal and yellow paint, with two eyes, one a spiral and one a white ring, and a small grin. The ears are two black points. A black shadow spreads under the head like spilled ink. The scribble here is black and heavy, and it covers the face so that the features are found inside it. The dark heads begin here, on November 23, 2022, and then the board went quiet for fifty-six days. A cat with a spiral eye was the first creature of the spring, drawn flat and humming on teal. This one is the same cat under a pile of black, and it is the last thing the artist drew before leaving for the winter.
A head on purple with spiky hair, two boxed eyes, and a yellow beam pouring from its mouth to the right, drawn in colored scribble over dark paint.

January 18 to February 15, 2023. Eight dark heads in scribble, with teeth bared, and one yellow figure with bones. The first was the collector's celebration purchase; the February ones were drawn as the burning was announced.

A dark head with two mouths of white teeth, one above the other, a red propeller for one eye and a yellow ring for the other, drawn in white, blue and red line over black. A black flower hangs at the upper right. The head is outlined in heavy white, and the two mouths fill the lower half. It is the first of the winter heads, drawn January 18, 2023, and the first with the teeth doubled. It was the first thing the artist posted after two months, and Jamie Thingelstad bought it that night for fifteen xDai, to celebrate, he wrote, that one of his favorite artists was publishing again. A head with two mouths is a head that has more to say than one mouth can hold. It came back from the winter talking twice.
A dark head in yellow, blue and black scribble with a blue X over one eye, a box of teeth where the other should be, and a grin of yellow teeth below.
A dark round head in scribble with one eye a red ring and the other a red oval, a grin of white teeth, and a white line running down the brow.

A tall dark head on brown, two hollow eyes with spiky lids, each with a small ring inside, a long dark nose, and a wide mouth of white teeth in red. The head is drawn in grey and brown scribble with a heavy black edge. Two months after the head on yellow in sixty-two strokes, this is the same head drawn in darkness: a box of a face, two eyes, a grin, with the ground gone black. The eyes are hollow and the lids are spiked, and the grin is clenched: it is the face of someone holding on. It was drawn on January 23, 2023, the same day as the woman in yellow light next door. The artist drew the softest person in the series and the hardest head on the same day.
A dark head in scribble with a ringed eye and a spiral eye, a mouth open on white teeth and a red tongue, on a ground of colored bars, from February 15, two days after the first burn notice.
A yellow figure in a frame with white bones sticking out of its head and shoulders, one arm raised, drawn in yellow and black line over a grey square.
A dense mask with two green hearts above the eyes, a ringed eye and a crossed eye, a grille of white teeth, on brown.
The last night. Four works between March 14 and 15, 2023, and then the collection piece, drawn last, bought that evening, and followed within hours by the whole series.
Three figures in a frame, a skull, a white skeleton and a pink robot, drawn in colored line over a crowded ground, with a small black figure at the lower right, the night before the last day.
A mask with a bird's head for one eye, its beak open on white teeth, a red ringed eye beside it, and a beam of red crossing from the upper right, on blue.
A figure with a sun for a head runs across red, in a blue shirt, one arm raised, drawn in red and white line over soft teal discs, running on the last day.
A round mask split in two, half yellow and half brown, with a ringed eye on each side, a red target for a mouth, in a frame of grey, drawn March 15, 2023, an hour before the collection piece.

The collection piece, an edition of one, drawn last on March 15, 2023. A crowd of figures from the series in one square: a black crow at the top, a skull head on a striped body, a yellow sun-face with a grin, a black cat with ex eyes, a blue skull in a ring, a small masked head. Every mark of the series is here, the beams, the X, the crown, the teeth. Where the first work of May 2022 packed a single mask to the frame, this one packs the whole series. That evening Jamie Thingelstad bought it for 300 xDai, the third origin piece he had bought in seven months, and in the hour around midnight UTC the artist sent the other sixty-three Rawblocks to his wallet, the one named for the board. In the two hours after drawing this, the artist painted two landscapes with no face in them, and they hang next door. Then the burning finished, and when the artist came back to the board months later the work had a new name and no series.

Look again at the head on yellow from November, sixty-two strokes of black line with the ground showing through, and then at the collection piece, where the square is full. The room went from one line to a crowd in four months, through a winter in which the artist burned the year's unsold inks and the heads got darker every week. The last of them is every creature of the series at once, and the night it was drawn the series went to the collector who had bought its first work on the day the market broke.

Two landscapes to end the wing. They were painted on March 15, 2023, in the two hours after the collection piece, and they are the last Rawblocks works. There is no head in either one. A sun sets through a stand of trees, and light falls through a forest onto a floor of fallen trunks. The artist had just finished a square with every creature of the series crowded into it, and then painted trees, twice, with more strokes than either of the series' origin pieces.

They hang here as a coda, apart from the rooms, because they look like nothing else in the series. The brushwork is the series' brushwork, soft discs of color with scribble and line over them, turned for once on trees and sky. That same evening the collector bought the collection piece and the series went to him, and in the days after, the unsold copies of the year's inks went to the burn address by the hundred. The last two things the artist painted before the fire were a sunset and a forest with the light coming through.
Both painted on March 15, 2023, the sunset first and the forest half an hour later, in the two hours after the collection piece.

A sunset through trees. A yellow sun blazes at the top with rays of pink, blue and yellow, and under it a stand of red-trunked trees with green crowns stands on a field of gold and orange, ruled with dark lines like a floor. The whole picture is painted in soft discs with scribble over them, and the sun's rays reach every corner. With 831 recorded strokes it is one of the two most worked drawings in the series. Ninety minutes after packing every creature of the year into the collection piece, the artist painted a sun with no face and trees with no one under them. In August the artist had written of a journey into the sun. This is the sun, reached, and it does not grin.

Light through a forest. Tall dark trees stand at the sides and a beam of pale light falls between them onto a clearing, where fallen trunks lie in the foreground painted in brown and red. Soft discs of white and lilac float in the light. Half an hour after the sunset, the light has moved from the sky to the ground, and the picture is dark except where it falls. With 1,061 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the Rawblocks, and the last. The beam is the searchlight of the whole collection, the one that lit the eyes in May and crossed the skulls in September, and here it falls on fallen trees in an empty wood. Nobody is in the picture. That is the last thing the series has to say, and it took more strokes than anything before it.

The sun in the first picture is the sun-face of the series without its face. Look at it once more, then at the forest, where the light falls on nothing but trees. That is where the Rawblocks end: with the mask set down, the crowd handed over, and the artist looking at the light.

Marks laid side by side until they build a surface. The twenty-five works in this room are bands, bars and washes: stripes of color stacked or crossed, blocks set in rows, grids drawn over soft fields. No faces, no figures. They were painted in one week, March 30 to April 4, 2022, on a different chain from everything else here, and the room follows the title numbers because the series carries no date for each work.

Two kinds of mark do most of the work. One is a broad vertical stroke, dragged down the square and left to drip, so that a picture is a row of poles or a curtain of color. The other is a thin straight line, drawn across or diagonally over the strokes, so that the surface becomes a plaid, a ladder or a grid. Behind nearly every set of bars is a soft field of color, grey, pink, maroon or cream, and the bars sit on it like rain on a window. After five months of teeth, the artist spent a week making pictures with nothing in them to look back.

They were made to be given away. On March 18, 2022, the artist posted the idea of a proof of support, something minted on another chain for everyone who held an ink, and on April 7 wrote that everyone should now have received their airdrop. Forty-four of the fifty-two paintings went to listed wallets: the board's builder got the first, danielsheldon the ninth, scrimshaw the sixth. The artist called it a small thank you for creating some value outside Nifty Ink. The calm in these pictures was aimed at particular people, and the record says who.
The first four numbers. Thick loops inside a square, a speckled field, a plaid of thin lines, and diagonals crossing a blotched ground. The first went to Austin Griffith, who built the board.

A square of pink and yellow on orange, and inside it thick loops of green and yellow drawn in rectangles, with thin lines of pink, white and purple running over them. The loops circle a dark center like a knot. The ground around the square is flat orange, and the pink inside it is soft and cloudy. It is the first of the Abstract works by number, and the only one in the room with a shape at its center. It was given to Austin Griffith, who wrote the software Nifty Ink runs on and who, two months earlier, had put ether into the artist's empty mainnet wallet. The first abstract went to the person who made the board. It is a knot, and it is warm.
A field of speckles in yellow-green, pink, blue and gold, with thin vertical lines rising through it like stems, and a band of magenta across the lower edge.
A plaid of thin blue, green and yellow lines over purple, with thick orange and yellow brush strokes laid across it at the left and lower center, and pink at the right edge.

Diagonal lines in red, green, blue and yellow cross the square from both corners over a ground of soft blotches in teal, grey and pink. A dark hairy cross sits at the upper left, and bunches of orange, blue and navy strokes lie scattered over the lines. It is the room's busiest surface, with four layers: the blotches, the thin diagonals, the thick strokes, and the hairy marks on top. The diagonals make an X across the whole square, the mark that cancels an eye in every other wing, here with no eye under it, and the picture is cheerful.
Numbers six to sixteen. Vertical strokes dragged down the square, soft washes behind them, and grids and bars drawn over. The sixth went to scrimshaw, whose heads hang in the last wing.
Dense colored dabs in blue, magenta, yellow and green, with dark bristly streaks running down through them like trunks; this is the one that went to scrimshaw.
Black lace of scribble over soft pink, yellow, mauve and olive, with thin horizontal lines through it.

Pale vertical bars in grey, tan and lilac, washed thin, with a band of orange and black across the middle like a railing seen through fog. The bars drip at their lower ends. Two dark poles stand at the left and the center, and a few thin lines are scratched into the wash at the upper right. It is the quietest picture in the room, and the first where the wash is the subject. It went to danielsheldon, one of the artists whose inks n n x y z liked most often on the board. A railing in fog, given to a painter: it is the nearest thing in the series to a letter.
Grey-blue bands washed over a dark ground, with small red and blue squares set along them like lights, and a pale bar at the upper right.
A green and beige wash ruled with thin lines into a grid, orange drips running down from the top, and turquoise at the corners.
Pink and grey vertical bands with a maroon stripe and a dark blue one, washed and splattered, with a pale blue block at the lower right.
Pale translucent blocks stand on maroon like windows, with yellow horizontal lines drawn across them, dashed and broken.

A patchwork of soft color: turquoise, orange, red, purple and yellow blocks laid side by side and overlapping, each one translucent, with darker drips falling through them. There is no line at all. The blocks are soft at every edge, and the color builds up where they cross, so the picture is deepest at the center and palest at the edges. It is the one work in the room with nothing drawn on it, only laid down, and it went to one of the wallets that bought the artist's inks most often on the board.
Pastel brush blocks in pink, yellow, lilac and olive with a purple band across the middle and white strokes laid over them.

Numbers twenty-five to thirty-four. Dark grounds with bright vertical bars, a pale one with rungs, and plaids of stripes and dabs. The artist was fighting the Polygon marketplaces that week and said so in a dozen posts; none of it shows here.
A soft patchwork of yellow, mauve, orange and green with black and white line scratched over it in loops and ladders.

Dark ground, and across it vertical bars of red, magenta and cyan, with a horizontal band of cyan near the bottom making a cross. The bars are brushy and bright against the dark, and they drip. A patch of pale pink hangs at the upper left like a lantern. It is the strongest contrast in the room, light bars on a near-black field, and the nearest the series comes to the dark grounds of the masks. Nothing in it has teeth. The dark is simply where the color is brightest.
Dark ground with vertical streaks of green, magenta, blue and yellow, a black column at the center, and a hatched band of fine lines along the bottom.
Pale grey bars washed down the square, with black rungs drawn across the right half like a ladder, and teal, red and yellow bars among the grey.

A cream ground, and on it a red circle at the lower left, blocks of yellow, blue, purple and grey, and thin black lines drawn across in a loose grid. A second circle at the upper right is drawn in line with a yellow half. The red circle is the one large shape in the room, and everything else on the page is arranged around it. A red sun low on a cream page, with a pale moon at the other corner: the room's one picture that could be a place, and it went to a wallet named ironsoul.
Red horizontal stripes on a pink ground, crossed by vertical bars of teal, yellow and grey, with black scratches over them.
On dark olive, yellow bars and squares with a diagonal yellow band across the lower half, pink dashes in a row across the middle, and fine lines like string.
Dense bars in red, teal and yellow, with rows of pink dots and white line scribbled over them in loops.
Two to end the room: a black grid with splatter, and a near-empty cream page with a few shapes on it. The last went to a collector who had bridged the artist's inks to Ethereum.

A grey ground ruled with thick black lines into a grid, and across the grid, splatter: black bursts at the upper left and lower right, and bars of red, blue and yellow set between the lines. Where the diagonals of number four made a net of thin lines, here the lines are thick, straight and few, and the marks sit inside the cells. A grid with something thrown at it is the room's picture of order and its opposite, and the splatter wins on points.

A cream page with a few shapes on it: a pink block at the left, a green block at the lower right, a red blob and a yellow blob at the top, a grey smudge, and thin black lines drawn in a loose frame around them. Most of the page is empty. It is the sparest work in the series, and the room ends on it. On April 13, 2022, the artist posted that number 49 was going, in three copies, to the collector who had upgraded the artist's inks from Gnosis to Ethereum. The emptiest painting in the series was the thank-you for the most expensive gesture a collector could make, and the artist chose it for that.

The plaid of thin lines near the start of the room and the cream page at the end, with its few blocks, were ruled by the same hand. One fills the square with lines until it is cloth. The other draws a frame and leaves the page bare. Both were gifts, and the quietest things the artist made were the ones the artist chose to hand to other people.

Marks thrown, dripped, scribbled and spun. The twenty-seven works in this room are the Abstract series at its loosest: splashes on a bare ground, crowds of short strokes, swirls that turn in a circle, lines that sweep across the square and leave. The room ends on the collection piece, number zero zero zero zero, which Jamie Thingelstad bought on May 3, 2023, and with it the fifty paintings that came with it, the fourth n n x y z collection he owned.

Three kinds of gesture hang here. The splash, which hits the ground and spreads. The scribble, which covers it. And the swirl, which turns the whole square into one motion, like a ball of yarn or a storm seen from above. All three are the marks the masks were made of, with the mask taken away: the scribble that buried the summer heads, the loops that drew the Faces, the beam that swept across the skulls, here allowed to be only themselves.

Look for the one face. Number thirty-eight is a skull drawn in loose loops over soft color, and it is the only face in the Abstract series. It went to dashmdash, one of the artists n n x y z liked most on the board. The series was painted in a week in the spring of 2022 and given away over the next two; a year later, with the unsold copies about to burn, the artist put the origin piece up and the collector took the whole set. The last painting the artist burned was never one of these.
Numbers five to twenty. Dots and splashes on dark or grey grounds, with lines scratched through them. Most went to wallets with no name, collectors known only by an address.

Dots of yellow, pink and cyan scattered over a dark marbled field, with white brush strokes dragged across the middle and bursts of pale yellow like fireworks. The field itself is streaked in green, blue and red, and the dots sit on top of it in drifts. It is the first gesture work by number, and it already has all three kinds: the splash, the scribble in the field, and the sweep of the white strokes. Fireworks over dark water is as close as the series comes to a subject, and the artist gave it to a collector with no name on the chain, which is most of who was there.
Red hatching in bunches over grey and green, with cyan and yellow line looping across it, and white hatching at the left.
Bright splashes of orange, blue, magenta and green on grey, with vertical dark streaks behind them and white bursts at the center.
A teal ground with pink and yellow lines scribbled across it, maroon splashes at the corners, and a white patch at the lower left.

A dark brown ground with a tangle of white line at the center, like a figure or a plant, and splashes of pink, yellow and red thrown around it. The white tangle is drawn in loops that climb from the bottom to the top. The splashes are soft and bright. It is the darkest ground in the room, and the one where the splash reads most like something thrown. The white tangle is a figure if you want it to be, with its arms up, and the splashes are what it is standing in. The series' one near-person is made of the same loops as its scribble.
Pink and cyan scratches over a soft blue and pink ground, with yellow strokes and black dashes, and a small figure at the lower right.
Numbers twenty-one to twenty-seven. The square fills with short strokes until it is a crowd, the way the first drawing of New Nifty on the Block filled with heads.
A dense crowd of short strokes in pink, teal, yellow and red, crossing in every direction, with rows of dots through them.
Dark ground with colored bars crossing it: yellow and purple vertical, white and grey diagonal, and tangles of fine line between them.

A brown ground filled edge to edge with short bars of color: red, yellow, cyan, pink, green and white, laid in a loose grid so that they read as a crowd of small flags. Black bars run among them. It is the brightest surface in the series and the most even, with no center and no empty corner. A crowd of flags with no one holding them: the block from the other wing, with the people gone and the colors left. It went to a collector with no name.
A textured mass of mauve, green, orange and yellow, drawn in fine scribble, with a block of pink at the lower left and black marks at the center.
Numbers thirty-five to forty. Strokes that turn in a circle, and in the middle of them the one face in the series, given to a fellow artist.
A grey haze with white and yellow strokes laid over it, a chain of dots running down the center, and black marks at the corners.
Dense colored scribble in pink, yellow, green and blue, with spirals drawn in it and black loops over everything, the Faces' tangle with no face found in it.

A swirl on blue: thick black and white strokes turn in a circle around a center of red and gold, with yellow and purple strokes caught in the turn. The black strokes are the longest marks in the series, curving from the top to the bottom edge. The whole picture moves in one direction, like water going down a drain. It went to darkking. A storm seen from above, or a drain, and the red and gold at the center is where everything is going. It is the most forceful painting in the series, and the only one that could be called angry, if a swirl can be.

A skull drawn in loose black loops over soft patches of red, green, blue and pink on white: two red eyes, a long nose, a row of teeth along the bottom. Thin black lines frame it. It is the only face in the Abstract series, and it hangs here because the loops that draw it are the loops of the swirls around it. It went to dashmdash, one of the artists n n x y z liked most often on the board, seventeen likes in the record. Fifty-two paintings with no face, and the one with a skull in it went to a fellow artist: the gift says the series knew what it was leaving out.
A brown mass hangs over a fire of red and orange strokes on grey, like smoke rising from flame.

Numbers forty-one to fifty, then the work titled pos, and the collection piece to end the wing. The pos edition was the ticket to the next airdrop; the collection piece was the key to all of it, bought by the collector in May 2023.

A field of grass-like strokes in blue, grey, white and yellow-green, standing up from the lower edge and leaning to the right, on white. The strokes are thin and close, like reeds. Blue is strongest at the left, green at the bottom. It is the one work in the room drawn entirely in vertical strokes, and the one that most looks like a place. Reeds in a wind on a white page, given to a wallet named godlessape, is the series at its most peaceful, and the wind is going somewhere.
On maroon, two crossed bars of gold and black at the center like a kite, with splashes of pink, teal and yellow around them.
On teal, splatter and drips in yellow, white, black and purple, with thin orange lines crossing the square.
Round dark blots on ochre, six of them, each drawn in circling strokes of teal and black like a thumbprint.

A swirl of yellow, black and grey-blue on grey, turning in a loose circle like a ball of yarn, with black dots caught in it. The strokes are short and curved, and they follow the turn. The grey ground shows all around. It is the lightest of the swirls, and the one with the clearest circle. Where the blue swirl was a storm, this one is yarn, and the difference is only how hard the hand came down. It was not on the list of gifts; it stayed with the artist until the collector bought the set.
Bright swirling strokes in magenta, yellow, cyan and black on grey, with a magenta loop at the center and white at the edges.
A soft pink and lilac haze with a single thin dark line drawn through it in a wandering path, down the right and across the bottom.
On yellow and white, a splash of black and color at the center dripping downward, with pink, green and purple caught in it.

A round mass of red, orange, teal and brown strokes on grey, drawn in circling layers like a burning ball, with drips running down from its lower edge. The strokes turn around a center and pile up until the mass is almost solid. The grey ground is scratched with grey lines. Its title is pos, the one Abstract work without a number. On April 12, 2022, the artist explained: pos stood for proof of support, and anyone who wanted the next airdrop had to hold a numbered abstract and one of these in the same wallet. It is a ticket, painted as a ball of fire. The artist's idea that year was that holding the work should be worth something, and this is what the idea looked like.

The collection piece, an edition of one. Yellow-green and magenta patches on a pale ground, black splatter thrown over them, and a tangle of thin orange, cyan and black lines drawn through the lower half, with a block of black scribble at the bottom. Loops, splashes and lines together. Where the first splash in this room threw dots on a dark field, this one throws its marks over a pale page and draws through them. On May 2, 2023, the artist posted that all unsold abstracts would be burned, and the next day Jamie Thingelstad bought this one on OpenSea and wrote that it came with all fifty of the collection, the fourth n n x y z collection he now had. Two months later the leftover copies went to the burn address. The one painting that holds every gesture of the series is the one that kept the series from the fire.

Look again at the first splash, dots on a dark field, and then at the collection piece, where splatter, patches and lines are all on one page. The room's three gestures end up together. The swirls between them are the series turning in place, and the one skull among the swirls is the artist unable, for one painting in fifty-two, to leave the face out.

Pieces made for a moment. The works in this room were drawn for occasions: the hundredth, two hundredth, three hundredth and five hundredth inks, a summer, a pizza day, a greeting. With them hang the few full figures and painted scenes from outside the named series. Twenty-two works, from the artist's first day on Nifty Ink in October 2021 to December 2024, the last drawing in the collection. This is the artist in public.

Most of them carry words. NIFTY INK on a tee shirt, WAGMI on a bottle, a number held up like a sign, slogans written across a face. The words are drawn, not typed, and they sit in the picture like any other mark. The milestones were never for sale: 200 nifties was minted straight into the wallets of collectors who had bought the inks, Jamie Thingelstad's among them, on April 25, 2022, the first n n x y z work he was given, and 300 nifties followed the same way in June. The artist celebrated by handing the celebration out.

Watch the sun-head. It appears in May 2022 as a figure with a sun for a face, in a NIFTY INK tee shirt, on a beach, in the dark, dancing, and the collector bought all three for a single xDai each. Two years later it comes back as a pizza. The room ends on two masks covered in writing from December 2024: dishwasher to memewasher, blue chip, sold by Christie's, no need for a wall. By then the artist had been posting for a year about the market as a rare-token scheme that had nothing to do with art, and these are the drawings that say it.

October 20, 2021, the first day of n n x y z on Nifty Ink: a figure in a cap and a river landscape. Then, in December, a dragon on the water. The collector bought the first two on August 11, 2022, the same day he bought most of the Scrimshaws, and received the dragon as a gift with the last Rawblocks in March 2023.

A figure in a blue cap and a yellow shirt, drawn in orange and white hatching with the letters N N X Y Z written in pink across its face, grinning with white teeth. The ground is a dense weave of red, green and blue hatching. The first n n x y z work on Nifty Ink, drawn October 20, 2021, and the name is already on the face. The artist's handle on every platform was four zeros and these five letters, and the first drawing wears them as a mask. Jamie Thingelstad bought it on the evening of August 11, 2022, for twenty xDai, the same night he bought the river below it and most of the Scrimshaws, and two nights before he bought the Faces origin piece. It was the week the artist announced the burning. The collector's answer was to go back to the beginning.

A river runs through a green valley under a sky of pink and white cloud, with a tree at the left and a stump at the right, all painted in soft strokes and scribble. Drawn six hours after the figure in the cap, on the same first day. It is a landscape without a face in it, and with 737 recorded strokes one of the most worked drawings in the wing. On the first day the artist drew the name, and then a river. The two landscapes that close the Rawblocks, seventeen months later, are this picture again, and this is where the collector started too: he bought it on August 11, 2022, for fifteen xDai, six hours before the cap.

A dragon rises from blue water, its head at the right, its body a long curve of gold and white strokes, its tail trailing across the dark sky. The water is a mass of cyan and white scribble like foam. The sky is black. It is the most densely drawn work in the whole collection, and the only dragon. It was drawn on December 7, 2021, the day before New Nifty on the Block began, and the artist sent it to the collector's wallet on March 28, 2023, a fortnight after the last handover, with the drawing for five hundred inks: two gifts, after everything else had gone, as if to finish the set. The dragon's name is Tolkien's. The artist, who never named an influence, named this one.

January to November 2022. Four milestone drawings for the hundredth, two hundredth, three hundredth and five hundredth inks, and three summer figures with a sun for a head. Two of the milestones were gifts to the collector; the summer figures cost one xDai each.

Three cartoon characters in green, blue and pink stand in a row with the letters X, Y and Z on their chests and the number 100 drawn above them in pale balloon letters. Their eyes are wide, their mouths open, and they drip at the feet into a grey floor. The milestone for the hundredth ink, made January 28, 2022, and the artist posted that it had been dropped into the pockets of some niftians. The three letters are the artist's name split into three people, and they are melting. The collector bought a copy in November 2022 for five xDai, after the series had ended, to have the first of the milestones.

Figures glow in a burst of light, drawn in gold and grey with a hand raised, and the words 200 NIFTY INK at the upper left; minted into the collector's wallet on April 25, 2022, the first n n x y z work he was given.

A figure with a sun for a head stands on blue in a white tee that says NIFTY INK, black shorts and sunglasses with X Y Z on the lenses, holding a bottle labeled WAGMI with bubbles rising from it. The sun is yellow with short rays. The arms and legs are yellow lines. The first of three summer figures, drawn May 10, 2022, the day after the market fell, and posted with a joke about Nifty Ink as a no-fuss printer. A sun in sunglasses with a bottle of champagne is a picture of a good mood held up against the news, and the collector bought it the morning it appeared, for one xDai, his first n n x y z purchase outside the Faces, three weeks after the first.
The same sun-headed figure at night, glowing in a ring of yellow on black, its tee grey, its arms out, bought the same evening for one xDai.
The sun-headed figure dances on teal in headphones, one leg kicked out, the word WAGMI floating around it with music notes and wavy lines, the third for one xDai, two days later.

A figure in black and white line with a visor and a grin holds a line that runs up to the signature, and a small figure at its feet holds up a sign that says 300; minted into the collector's wallet on June 20, 2022, with many others.

A face in dense colored line on orange: a long nose, two glasses-like rings, dark hair falling at the sides, a small closed mouth, drawn in black, yellow, blue, white and red strokes over a painted face. It is the milestone for the five hundredth ink, drawn November 12, 2022, and it is a portrait, not a cartoon. The first three milestones were cartoons and this one is a tired person with their mouth shut, drawn the day after FTX filed for bankruptcy, in the week of the Rawblocks portraits. The artist sent it to the collector in March 2023, with the dragon. Five hundred drawings in, the celebration is a face that has stopped celebrating.

Six numbered works from November 2023 to March 2024 that are figures, not masks: a dancing girl, a rabbit, a hooded figure, a crouching creature, a pair, and a creature with hearts. After the series ended, the artist was still drawing for an audience that had mostly left, and the collector was still there.
A girl with orange curly hair and pink cheeks dances in a teal frame, her arms drawn in blue loops, a shower of yellow and blue dots falling at the left.

On pink, a black figure walks at the left, a red rabbit stands at the center with ringed eyes, and a dark figure with a white smile stands at the right under a yellow sun with a face. Yellow bars float behind them. The three figures are drawn in different ways, the first in black with a yellow face, the rabbit in red scribble, the third in black with a tangle of yellow line. It is the one crowd scene in the room, drawn December 28, 2023, in a run of eight drawings in three days. A year after the series ended, three figures walking in the sun on pink: the block, with three people left on it.
A hooded figure painted in dark brown against orange and gold, its face lost in the hood, thin lines ruled across the whole square.
A black creature with a crown of spikes and a grin of teeth crouches on yellow, drawn in black and blue scribble, hatched lines at the right.
Two figures on teal, one in a cap and one with red ex eyes and a red beam, drawn in dark scribble with white line over them.

A green and red creature in sunglasses with a mouth of teeth stands on purple, with three red hearts beside it, each with a small face, and a dark figure in a cap on a pole at the right. A sad sun looks down from the top. Blue raindrops fall. The hearts have faces, the sun has a face, and the creature has sunglasses: everything in the picture looks at something. It was drawn on March 20, 2024, two days before the artist posted that success in our society is not tied to hard work. Three hearts with worried faces, a sad sun, rain, and a creature in sunglasses grinning through it: the picture is a mood, and the mood is the post.
May to December 2024. Three pizza drawings in two days, a pink head, and two masks covered in words. The pizza drawings were bought for one and two xDai.

A pizza slice for a head, with red glasses and a grin, under a yellow sun with a face, drawn in orange and gold hatching with yellow rays over everything. Two years after the sun-headed summer figures, the sun is back, and the figure under it has become a slice of pizza. The first of three pizza drawings, made May 19, 2024, two years after the first summer figure. Bitcoin Pizza Day, May 22, is the anniversary of the first thing ever bought with the coin, and the artist, who had spent the month posting that the market was a scheme, drew pizza for two days ahead of it, a grinning slice in glasses first. The collector bought all three for one or two xDai each.
A round head on black with pizza slices on top like a crown, blue glasses, a grin of white teeth, and a slice of pizza on its white shirt, the crown of the last masks made of pizza.
A man in red glasses and a red cape stands in blue rain holding up a sign with hearts, a pizza flying at the upper right and a small creature at his feet.

A face inside a black frame, covered in words: DIGITAL ART in pink, BLUE CHIP in blue, OG, and a line about going from dishwasher to memewasher along the top. The face has a red crossed eye, a grin of white teeth and a yellow hook of a nose. Green and blue scribble fills the rest. The words are drawn in as many hands as colors. Drawn December 4, 2024, after seven months away from the board. They are the words of the market the artist had been writing against all year: rich, rich, rich; blue chip; OG. The face wearing them has one eye crossed out and is grinning, and the frame around it is the wall the next drawing says there is no need for.

A mask with a pink flower for an eye and a grin of teeth, under the words NO NEED FOR A WALL in yellow and black, with memewasher, artfluencer and sold by Christie's written around it in white, pink and red. Drawn the day after the framed face, December 5, 2024. It is the last work in the collection by date, and it is mostly writing. A flower for an eye is the gentlest eye in the collection, and the mask that wears it is surrounded by the vocabulary of the trade: influencer, auction house, meme. No need for a wall is the artist's last sentence on the board as far as this collection goes, and it can be read two ways, as a boast about digital art and as a shrug about galleries. This gallery takes it as both, and hangs it on a wall.

A related item from the Scrimshaw collection: the letters G and M drawn in looping colored line on a muddy ground, a greeting by the artist Scrimshaw, dated November 2021. It hangs here with the occasion pieces because it is one.

Look again at the first figure, with the artist's name written across its face in October 2021, and then at the last, a mask under a slogan in December 2024. Three years apart, and both are faces made partly of words. The first says who the artist is. The last says what the artist thought of the business the first one walked into, and both are grinning.

The masks of 2023 and 2024. After the named series ended, n n x y z kept drawing heads, and these twenty-three are the numbered ones: packed faces with teeth, crowns and crossed eyes, drawn between July 2023 and May 2024. They are denser than the earlier masks, and the line is heavier. The numbers start again at one, as if the year of series had never happened, and the artist posted each one with its place in the count of all the inks: number 44, ink 569.

Most of them have a beam. A bar of yellow or red crosses the face at eye height, or shoots from one eye to the edge. Under it the face is built the old way, from boxes and rings and a grille of teeth, but the scribble over it is now thick enough to be a surface of its own. The audience had mostly gone. The board was quieter, the market was a scheme the artist posted about with disgust, and the drawings came a few a month for whoever was still looking. One collector was: Jamie Thingelstad bought nearly every one of these, usually for five xDai, often in batches on a single night.

The ground changes under the masks. In the first it is white or grey. By December 2023 it is green, purple and gold, and the last masks of spring 2024 stand on red, blue and orange. In February 2024 the artist wrote that the need to create art and the need to make art for its own sake are two different intentions, one to express something and the other to express yourself. These masks are the second kind, made for no occasion and no series, and they are the heaviest in the collection.

July and August 2023. Four heads to begin: a dark head in glasses on white, two crowned masks, a round scribbled head, and a skull on stripes. The collector bought the first in August and the next three on one night in September, five xDai each.

A dark head in round glasses on white, its skull a weave of colored scribble, a grin of white teeth across the whole jaw, and a yellow beam crossing behind the glasses. The glasses are two yellow lenses in dark rings. The teeth are drawn large, each one outlined, in a row that runs past the edges of the face. The first numbered mask, from July 18, 2023, with 423 recorded strokes, four months after the Rawblocks ended and the burning finished. The artist came back to the board with the count reset to one and drew the mask again, in glasses, on a white page, grinning as wide as the face. The collector bought it on August 6, for five xDai, into the wallet he had named for the artist.
Two masks side by side in red, black and yellow scribble, the left one crowned, with a red X over one eye and a grin of white teeth, the right one smaller with a box of teeth.
A round head in dense yellow, green and blue scribble on grey, with a ringed eye at the left, a box eye at the right, and a mouth of white teeth in a red box, a yellow bar across the top.
A skull mask on red and pink stripes, drawn in blue, orange and white line, with a target eye, a grille of white teeth and a red heart at the lower right.
November 2023. A patterned boxy mask with hearts, a brown one with red crosses, a white-outlined head with its tongue out, and a dark mask lit by a beam.

A boxy mask on grey, packed with pattern: a red X eye, a box eye, a grille of teeth, two red hearts at the lower center, a cup at the left, and a second small face at the upper left with its own grin. Blue, red and yellow line runs over the whole in loops and ladders. It is the busiest mask in the room, drawn November 2, 2023, with 225 strokes. Two hearts and a cup of coffee under a cancelled eye: the mask has a domestic life now, and the small second face at the corner is company. The collector received it that month.
A brown boxy mask with two red crosses in its eyes and a mouth of white and black bars, drawn in black and blue line on brown, with a pink flower at the top.

A head outlined in thick white on black, its face a mass of colored scribble, with two red star eyes, a red mouth open on white teeth and a long red tongue hanging out. The outline is one heavy white loop around the whole head and shoulders. The tongue is the brightest thing in the picture. It is the one mask in the room with its mouth open wide, drawn November 15, 2023. A tongue out is a child's rudeness, and the star eyes are a cartoon's, and the heavy white outline holds them like a sticker on black. It is the rudest and the happiest head of the year, and the collector took it with the two before it.
A dark mask on yellow and olive, with a yellow crossed eye at the right, a beam of orange shooting from it, a grid of lines over everything and a red mouth of white bars.

December 28 to 30, 2023. Eight masks in three days: rays, a crown, a flower eye, a pink hand, a yellow cap, small skulls, red hands, and a head in beams. The collector bought most of them in one sitting on April 10, 2024.
A mask in a field of yellow and orange rays, with two ringed eyes, a grin of white teeth in a red mouth, and purple strokes like lashes.
A mask on purple outlined in thick white with a scalloped edge, a crown of white spikes, a box eye, a bar across the brow, and a grille of white teeth in red.

A dark mask on green with a crest of black spikes, a blue flower for one eye and a box with a ring for the other, a red beam from the left, and a grin of white teeth. Rows of red hearts run down the right edge. The flower eye is drawn with pointed blue petals around a yellow center. It is the first of eight masks drawn in three days at the end of December 2023. A flower for an eye returns a year later on the last work in the collection; here it is next to a beam and a row of hearts, and the mask looks, for once, pleased to be looked at.
A dark mask on purple with a pink hand pressed to the top of its head, two ringed eyes, and a grin of white teeth in a red mouth, yellow line around.
A head in a yellow cap on grey, its face a cage of white and red line with two ringed eyes and a grin of white teeth, in seventy-two strokes.

A grey skull mask with a pink hand and a crossed eye at the left, a box of teeth in red, and five small white skulls floating at the right, each with its own face. A red beam crosses from the left. The small skulls are drawn in black line on white, like a crowd of ghosts watching. It is the one mask with company, drawn December 29, 2023. The five small skulls are an audience, and they are skulls: whoever is still watching the artist draw at the end of 2023 is drawn as the dead, politely attentive. The collector, who was watching, bought it in April.
A mask with a red crossed eye and a spiral eye, a grin of white teeth, and two red hands raised at the bottom corners, on dark blue.

A dark head lit by beams of gold from the upper right, its face painted in yellow and brown with a grin of teeth, two hands raised, and a row of gold bars at the lower left like coins. Pink and green dashes float in the dark. The light is the subject: it falls across the head and the hands and leaves everything else black. With 517 recorded strokes it is the most worked mask in the room, drawn on December 30, 2023, the last of the eight. Gold light, raised hands and a stack of coins: it is either a saint or a man being robbed, and the grin does not settle it. The beam from the summer of 2022 is back, and it has found the money.

February to May 2024. Seven last masks: a framed crown, a skull on red, glasses on green, goggles on blue, curly hair, a man with a beam, and a hatted scream. The artist spent May posting about the market as a scheme, and drew these.
