A crowned yellow mask in a black frame with green spikes, two spiral eyes, a grin of white zigzag teeth, and two small black figures at the lower corners.
A skull mask on red drawn in thick white line, with a ringed eye, a crown of purple spikes, a mouth of white loops, and a yellow bar across the top.
A mask in square glasses on green, a yellow beam crossing behind the lenses, a grin of white teeth, two hands raised, drawn in black and orange scribble.
A blue skull mask in goggles with a crossed eye between the lenses, a yellow beam, a grille of white teeth, and a crown of black spikes, on blue.
An orange mask with curly yellow hair, a flower for one eye and a black spiral for the other, a grille of white teeth, drawn in white and black line.

A man in glasses with spiky yellow hair on red, drawn in dark scribble with pink and blue inside, a yellow beam shooting from his glasses to the upper right, one hand raised. The face is more a person than a mask: a nose, a mouth, glasses that sit on the nose. Ten months after the first numbered head in glasses, the glasses are back, and the beam that crossed behind them now leaves from them. It was drawn on May 8, 2024, in the week the artist posted that the rare-token business had nothing to do with art and that everyone should get out early. A man in glasses with a beam coming out of his eyes and his hand up is someone with something to say, and the artist that week had plenty.

A head in a brown hat screams on teal, its mouth wide open on white teeth, its eyes shut, its hands at its ears, painted in olive and gold with scribble over it. The hat is drawn in dark brown with a wide brim. The mouth is the largest in the room. It is the last numbered mask, drawn May 30, 2024, and the collector bought it on June 23, for five xDai, with the little abi ninja head. The eyes are shut and the hands are at the ears: this is not a scream at someone, it is a scream with the world shut out. Three years of grins end on a face that has stopped pretending the grin was the point, and it was the last of these heads anyone bought.

The first head wears glasses and grins on white. The last screams in a hat on teal. Both are heads with their mouths open. One is a mask with the scribble on top. The other is a face, painted, with its eyes shut, and after three years of grinning it is the collection's last word: a scream, bought by the one collector still on the board, a month after it was drawn.

Heads by Scrimshaw, a different artist. These twenty-five works are the earliest in the collection, most of them drawn on February 16, 2021, the rest over the following days, with a few returns as late as December 2023. They hang together because they share one way of drawing: a head built from loose, looping colored line, on a bright ground. They were on the board eight months before n n x y z's first ink, and they bare their teeth the same way.

The line is the whole method. A head is a loop, then another loop in another color, then a third, until the face is a weave of blue, red and yellow lines that never quite close. Eyes are rings. Teeth are zigzag. Hair is a crest of straight strokes. Who saw whom is not in the record, and the gallery does not guess. What the record holds is a thread: n n x y z liked three of Scrimshaw's inks on the board, and in April 2022 Scrimshaw received the sixth of the Abstract paintings as a gift. Two artists who drew a mouth the same way, and one of them said thank you in paint.

The collector is the other thread. Jamie Thingelstad bought the greeting GM in April 2022, three weeks before his first n n x y z purchase, and then, on two evenings in August 2022, bought twenty-one of these heads within ten minutes each night: the first night was the one he bought the first two n n x y z drawings, and the second was the day before he bought the Faces origin piece. He has said he sees a related visual character in Scrimshaw. The wall agrees. Watch the halos: several heads have a ring or an oval drawn above them, and it is one of the marks that sets these apart from the n n x y z masks in the other wings.

February 16, 2021, from the afternoon to midnight. Ten drawings in seven hours, from a pale face in blue line to a long-haired face in pink. The collector bought all ten on the evening of August 11, 2022, Minneapolis time, within five minutes.

A face drawn in one blue line over a pale ground of yellow and lilac discs, with a square chin, two small eyes and a zigzag of teeth, a crest of blue strokes above. The line wanders from the brow down the nose to the jaw and back, and the pale color behind it is laid in soft overlapping shapes. It is the earliest work in the whole collection, from the afternoon of February 16, 2021, when Nifty Ink was six months old. The face is calm and the teeth are a zigzag. Before n n x y z drew a single ink, this mouth was on the board, drawn by someone else, and the collector bought it eighteen months later on the night he began buying n n x y z in earnest.
A skull drawn in looping blue, white and yellow line on blue, with ringed eyes and a mouth of purple teeth, vertical strokes falling around it like hair.

Three heads outlined in thick black line on purple, side by side, their faces filled with orange, white and blue scribble, their noses and mouths drawn in a few black strokes. The black outline runs around all three without a break. It is the first drawing in the collection with more than one face, and the one where the line is heaviest. Three heads in one outline is a family or a band, and the grins are mild. Ten months later n n x y z drew a crowd of heads for the first New Nifty on the Block, in a different hand, with more teeth.
A face in dark purple line on light blue, with ringed eyes, a red mouth of teeth, and a crest of purple strokes, drawn in sixty-nine strokes.

A skull face on yellow framed in red line, with a cross on its brow, two ringed eyes in red and blue, a mouth of white zigzag teeth, and green hair drawn in straight strokes. Blue zigzag runs across the lower half. The red frame is a box drawn around the head in a few strokes. The face is a skull, but with hair and a frame it is also a portrait. The ringed eyes, the zigzag teeth, the red frame: three of the parts n n x y z would build a year of masks from are on this one yellow square from February 2021. The gallery states the date and stops there.

Three narrow figures stand together in a field of orange, their upright bodies assembled from red, blue, white and yellow lines. Looking can alternate between three characters and one interwoven pattern. They have halos, or hats, drawn as loops above the heads, and they are the first standing figures in the collection.
A painted face in brown on yellow with long hair, two blue-ringed eyes and a small mouth, blue line drawn over the paint.

A large head nearly fills the square, assembled from thick red, black and yellow lines. Its eyes receive different frames: a purple ring on one side and orange loops on the other. Yellow and blue ovals organize the dark mouth into repeated rows. Two eyes that do not match and a mouth of ovals in rows: of all the Scrimshaw heads this is the one that most resembles the n n x y z masks, and it was drawn in February 2021. The title repeats a number, and the collection keeps both.
A pale face with a spiral drawn above it, rays of red and purple fanning from the spiral, two ringed eyes and a mouth of white zigzag teeth.
A face with long black hair drawn in straight strokes over pink and teal lines, on yellow, a pink halo above, the face a few black strokes.
February 17 to 22, 2021. A faint face on orange, a haloed face on purple, a grid of sixteen faces, and three more heads.
A faint face in white, blue and yellow line on orange, tipped to the right, with blue strokes for hair, in fifty-two strokes.
A face with long black hair drawn in straight strokes over pink and teal lines, on yellow, a pink halo above, the face a few black strokes.

Sixteen faces in a grid of four by four on purple, each drawn in loose black and white line with a different expression: one grins, one frowns, one has a mouth of teeth, one looks sideways. The grid lines are drawn by hand. It is the most densely drawn work in the Scrimshaw collection, and the only grid. Sixteen moods on one page, drawn in a sitting on February 18, 2021: it is the room's clearest statement that the face was the subject and the expression was the game, and the same game n n x y z would play across three hundred masks.

A face with a wide black ring above it like a hat, drawn in black, red and blue line on pale green, with a target eye and an X eye, a red mouth and a spiral at the chin, the X and the target in one face in February 2021.
A blue head on yellow with a crest of blue strokes, two ringed eyes, and a mouth open on black zigzag teeth, a spiral at the upper right.
A long-haired face on blue with red and purple hair falling in long strokes, two ringed eyes with crosses, and a mouth of black zigzag teeth.
March to August 2021. Five figures standing together, a boxed face, a spiky head, a crossed eye, and two heads on black.

Five upright figures stand close together, their long colored bodies filling the square. Thin lines cross between them, while differences in facial marks and color keep each figure distinct. Loops above their heads repeat the same gesture across the group. The title is an instruction, from March 2021, a year before the market fell, and it is the gentlest picture in the wing: five people in a row, each a different color, holding still together. The collector bought it on August 12, 2022, the day after n n x y z began burning the unsold inks.
A boxed face on orange drawn in purple, blue and yellow line, two ringed eyes, a mouth of zigzag, and a spiral at the chin, with loops running out past the box.
A spiky-haired head on yellow, drawn in black, red and blue line, with a ringed eye, a long nose and a mouth of white teeth, in sixty-nine strokes.

A face on purple with one eye crossed out in yellow, a ringed eye beside it, and a grin of white teeth, drawn in dense purple, red and yellow scribble with a cloud of black loops above for hair. It is the most worked drawing in the Scrimshaw collection, with 320 recorded strokes, and the crossed eye is drawn as a yellow X in a red ring. May 11, 2021: an eye cancelled with an X, a grin, and a head buried in scribble, five months before n n x y z arrived on the board. The gallery does not say n n x y z saw it. It says it was there.
Two heads on black, drawn in pink, purple and yellow line, facing each other, with a red loop between them like a handle.

Four works from August to December 2023, two and a half years after the rest: a dark head with a red mouth, a face with a third eye, a brown face on black, and a crowned skull. The collector bought each within days of its appearing.

A dark head on grey with green hair, a crossed eye, a red mouth of teeth, and colored scribble inside the face, drawn in black and purple line; the collector bought it the day after it appeared, in August 2023.

A face on teal with one ringed eye at the left, a blue eye at the right, a third eye drawn on the forehead in a diamond, and a mouth of black bars, drawn in orange, pink and blue line over a soft ground. A black hook hangs from the left ear. The title is Wobbler, and the face leans to the left as if it might. Drawn in October 2023, when n n x y z was drawing the numbered masks a few a month and the board was quiet; the collector bought it ten days later. The third eye is new. The mouth of bars is the old one.
A brown face on black drawn in white and black loops, two ringed eyes and a third ring above, a mouth of white zigzag teeth, in seventy-two strokes.

A skull in profile on black, facing left, drawn in pink, cyan, yellow and red line, with a yellow crown floating above it and a ringed eye, its teeth a row of yellow and orange bars. The line is thick and clean, every color separate. It is the last work in the Scrimshaw collection, from December 14, 2023, and where the first face was one blue line on a pale ground, this one is a dozen colors on black. A crowned skull in profile on black is also, almost exactly, the collection piece of New Nifty on the Block, drawn fourteen months earlier by the other artist. The collector bought it three days later. The gallery notes the rhyme and leaves the two artists to it.

Look again at the first face, one blue line over pale color, drawn on a February afternoon in 2021, and then at the crowned skull on black from December 2023. The line got thicker and the ground got darker. The loops stayed. The last head wears a crown, like the last n n x y z masks of 2022, and the gallery leaves it at that: two artists, one board, one mouth, and a collector who hung them in the same house.

What the artist sent to the people who held the inks. In the spring and summer of 2022 n n x y z used a second chain, Polygon, where minting cost almost nothing, to make things for collectors on the drawing board: a pixelated twin for every Nifty Face a person held, a club of flat cartoon cats, a few one-off pieces dropped into the wallets of the buyers who had kept coming back. Twenty works, April to October 2022, and every one of them arrived unasked for.

On April 21, 2022, the artist promised that once the Faces reached 130, every holder would receive the matching pixelated version, number one the same as the original and all the others changed a little so each was unique. On May 4 the artist posted that everyone should now have theirs. Six of the Faces in the second wing have their twins here, and the twin of the Faces origin piece arrived in October, seven weeks after the collector bought the original. The cats came in July, when the artist wrote that every holder of an ink should by now have a chic city cat, and then sold the rest for one MATIC each; the collector bought ten in one evening.

These are the artist's thank-you notes, and they are drawn in a different hand from the inks: flat vector shapes, pixel grids, no scribble. Look at the twins beside the Faces they copy, if you know them. The same grin, with the line taken out and the grid put in, is still a grin.
April 28, 2022. Two pieces the artist dropped into the collector's wallet on one day: the only survivor of an eight-piece Polygon set, and a pixel figure from a series called pxlpop.

A tall dark figure in magenta and red scribble on black, drawn in a vertical frame twice as high as it is wide: a head, a long body, thin lines running down like rain. It is the one survivor of a Polygon contract the artist called simply n n x y z, eight pieces minted, seven of them burned by the artist afterwards. The collector received it on April 28, 2022, three days after the artist first minted a milestone drawing into his wallet on the drawing board. A figure in the dark, drawn tall for a phone, is the first thing n n x y z made for him off the board, and it is the loneliest picture in the wing.

A pixel figure with blond hair in a blue jacket and dark trousers stands against a brown gradient scattered with stars, drawn on a coarse grid like a character from a 1990s game. The artist posted on May 8, 2022, that a pxlpop had gone as a second little airdrop to a collector who kept filling his pockets with the inks; this one went to Jamie Thingelstad ten days earlier, on April 28. It is the artist's pixel style before the Faces got theirs, and the figure is standing at ease with its hands at its sides, the only relaxed body in the room.

May 1 to 4, 2022. Six Faces the collector held were sent their pixelated twins within days of the artist's promise. Each is the drawing redrawn on a grid, the colors kept and the line replaced by squares.

A mosaic of a mask: boxed eyes, a grille of white teeth, a yellow crown of spikes, the whole square filled with colored tiles on green. It is Nifty Faces number 105 turned into pixels, drawn, in the artist's words, so that every Face a person held got its matching twin. The collector received it on May 1, 2022, the day after the artist had finished sending them. Look at the original in the Faces wing and then at this: the scribble that made the face is gone, and the tiles do the same work with no line at all. The grin survives the translation, which says something about how little it ever depended on the line.
A head in a wide hat on orange, in tiles of brown, black and yellow, with a grille of white teeth and a red cross over one eye, the twin of Faces number 125.

A dark head in sunglasses on grey, the mouth a wide grille of white tiles, red at the corners, the twin of Faces number 159 and the one that looks most like a photograph that has been enlarged too far.

An angry mask on dark red: two red eyes under heavy brows, a crown of orange spikes, a grille of white teeth, all in tiles. The original, Faces number 160, hangs in the room of skulls in the dark. On the grid the anger reads at a glance: the brows are two dark diagonals, the eyes two red squares, and nothing softens them. The artist wrote that every twin got minor changes, making each unique. Here the change is the grid itself, which makes the face harder, as if a snarl had been set in tile.
A round head on dark green with a cigarette, two spiral eyes and a wide grin, the tiles in yellow, red and white, the twin of Faces number 175.
A face on teal in brown and white tiles with a grille of teeth and a tall forehead, the twin of Faces number 179, and the plainest of the six.

July 15 to October 15, 2022. Eleven chic city cats: three sent free to the collector as a holder of the inks, seven bought for one MATIC each on August 21, and one that arrived on the day New Nifty on the Block ended.

A blue cat sits in profile on a grey ledge, its body striped in pale blue, its tail curled pink, against a ground split on the diagonal between teal and a darker blue. The eyes are two X marks. It is one of the first chic city cats, number 6 of nearly ten thousand, and it came to the collector on July 15, 2022, the day the artist posted that everyone who held an ink should by now have received a cat. The club was the artist's answer to a promise made in May, when the cats of the spring were still black silhouettes on the board; here the cat is flat, blue and sitting still, and the ex eyes are the only thing it kept from the drawings.
A cyan cat in a pink cap with a heart on it, sitting on a split ground of orange and brown, sent to the collector on July 18.

A violet cat with white stripes and a pink tail, ex eyes, on a split ground of green and teal, sent to the collector on July 28, the day the artist posted that every owner of an ink should now be the proud owner of a chic city cat.

A lime green cat with a black tail sits on a split ground of maroon and brown, one eye a target, the mouth a small grin. The collector bought it on August 21, 2022, in one transaction with five others, at one MATIC each, the price the artist had set for anyone who wanted to mint a cat for themselves. Nine days earlier the artist had announced that the year's unsold inks would burn. The cats were the opposite of a burn: nearly ten thousand of them, for a dollar, sent to whoever wanted one. The collector wanted ten.
A dark grey cat with white stripes on a split ground of slate and blue, bought with number 194.
A pale grey cat with spiral eyes on a split ground of olive and brown, bought the same evening.
A pink cat with white stripes and a heart for one eye on a split ground of purple and green, bought the same evening.
A lavender cat with a white hoop earring on a split ground of orange and brown, bought the same evening.

A cat whose body fades from pink at the head to orange at the tail, with a ball of yarn at its feet, on a split ground of blue and olive. It is the one cat in the room drawn in a gradient, and the one that has something to play with. The collector bought it on August 21 in a second transaction, with three more. Four hundred is a round number, and the artist was by then numbering the inks toward four hundred and announcing their burning; the cat with the same number is pink and has a toy.
A grey cat with a halo and ex eyes on a split ground of teal and green, bought with number 400, the one cat that is both dead and blessed.

A cyan cat with a halo sits on a split ground of purple and green, its eyes two small marks, its tail white. It came to the collector on October 15, 2022, the Saturday the artist drew the last three works of New Nifty on the Block, and the day before the whole of that series was sent to him. A cat with a halo on the day the series ended: the artist, who had just drawn a crowned skull as the collection piece, sent the collector a small blessed cat the same afternoon. Nothing in the record says it was meant as a sign, and it is hard to look at it as anything else.
October 4, 2022. The pixel twin of the Faces origin piece, sent seven weeks after the collector bought the original.

The Faces origin piece in tiles: a dark square packed with blocks of red, blue, yellow and white, the artist's name spelled across it in pixels where the original spelled it in scribble, a grille of white teeth low in the frame. The collector bought Nifty Faces number zero zero zero zero on August 13, 2022, for five hundred xDai, and on October 4 the artist sent him its twin, the only pixel twin that was not part of the May airdrop. The twins were made for everyone who held a Face. This one was made for the one person who held the Face that held all the others, and it closes the room the way the original closes its wing: a name, a grin, and the whole series packed in behind them.

The room begins with a dark figure drawn on a phone in April and ends with the pixel twin of the Faces origin piece in October. In between are six Faces turned into mosaics and eleven cats that cost a dollar. None of it was for sale on the board; it was what the artist did for the people who stayed, and the collector who stayed longest has the fullest set.

What the artist made after the inks, on every chain the collector followed. In August 2022, with the year's drawings about to burn, n n x y z announced an open, never-ending collection, published independently on several blockchains and expanded by one work each time the last one sold out, and named it the index collection after Andy Warhol's Index Book. Its first work, a hooded red face called Heaven or Hell, is here four times, on Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum and Tezos: one picture, four chains, which was the point. Twenty-six works, August 2022 to March 2024.

The rest is the artist trying things. Fields of colored noise and a grid of dots sold under a contract the artist named GenAI. A lake, a crowd of dancing skeletons, a rainbow summer and a shrine, made with the generative tools the artist defended in a post of August 2022: why should an artist disclose the tools he uses, since when are artists the slaves of their tools. Two scribbled heads on black that could have come from the board. Seven flat portraits of men in hats and masks called Friends of Country Air. The drawing hand is here once or twice; mostly it is the same mind choosing from a new box of tools.

The collector was there for all of it. He minted Heaven or Hell on Ethereum, Optimism and Arbitrum on the day each opened, bought the lake and the noise fields in the week FTX fell, and kept a Tezos wallet the artist sent work to for two years. The artist wrote in 2024 that the need to create art and the need to make art for its own sake are two different intentions, one to express something and the other to express yourself. This room is where the second kind lives, and the words the artist attached to it are the plainest the record has: an artist's life can be heaven or hell; create, try, hope, die, game over, repeat.

August 2022. The first work of the index collection, minted by the collector on Ethereum, Optimism and Arbitrum on August 6, the day each chain opened, and sent to his Tezos wallet by the artist in November and December 2023.

A face in a hood of white and pale pink, the face itself a deep red, scrawled over with yellow marks that are the artist's tag, on a near-black ground scattered with color. The picture is an animation of eleven frames; the marks and the hood shift from one to the next. Its title is Heaven or Hell, and the artist's description on the token says an artist's life can be heaven or hell, depending on the circumstances and the current contemporary culture, you can make it or die trying. It is the first work of the index collection, the open-ended series the artist announced on August 2, 2022, priced at five dollars so that, in the artist's words, people would show they wanted it. The collector minted this copy on Ethereum on August 6, the day the artist opened the collection there. A hooded red face with a name written over it, published so it could be bought on any chain: it is the artist's self-portrait as a product, and the title is a shrug with the whole year behind it.
The same animation minted on Optimism, number three of the collection there, on the same day, for the same five dollars.
The same animation on Arbitrum, the third chain the collector minted it on that day, so that the one picture sat in three wallets on three networks before the week was out.

The same face a fourth time, on Tezos, where the artist had published the index collection in August 2022 in an edition of twenty-five. The artist sent three copies to the collector's Tezos wallet on November 15, 2023, and three more on December 11: six, which is more than anyone needs of one animation and exactly what a collector who had been following the artist across chains for eighteen months was owed. The index collection's description says it was planned completely openly. Four copies of its first work, on four chains, in one collection, is what open looks like when someone takes the artist at their word.

October and November 2022. A scribbled figure on Tezos, a painted lake called oink, five fields of colored noise, a field of stripes, and a grid of dots, the last of them under a contract the artist named GenAI. The collector bought the lake and the noise fields in the week FTX collapsed.

A dark figure with a mane of colored strokes standing out from its head, a beam of gold across its eyes, on black: four frames that flicker. It was minted on Tezos on October 3, 2022, the morning the artist drew three crying portraits on the drawing board, and it came to the collector's Tezos wallet from the artist on October 11. It is the drawing hand at work on a new chain: the spiky hair, the beam, the scribble, all from the board, in an animation the board could not make. The collector had opened the Tezos wallet in August 2022 and the artist sent work to it for two years. This was the first.

A lake under trees, painted soft and wide, the water pale blue, the trees a blur of green and brown, the sky white. There is nothing in the picture with teeth. The artist put it on Optimism under a contract named simply n n x y z, called it oink, and the collector bought it on November 7, 2022, for three hundredths of an ether, the day after the run on FTX began. In the week the collector was buying the artist's frightened portraits on the board, he also bought this, a lake with no one in it, from the same artist on another chain. The title is a pig's noise. The picture is the calmest thing n n x y z ever sold.

A square of fine colored noise: thousands of tiny dots in grey, red, blue and yellow, with no shape in them, like a television between channels. It is one of a series the artist called opticals, sold on Optimism for a hundredth of an ether; the collector minted four on November 17, 2022, the week FTX filed for bankruptcy. The Tezos copies of the same series sit under a contract the artist named GenAI. After a year of faces, the artist sold pictures with no face, no figure and no mark of a hand, and gave them a name that means something to look at. Stand back and the noise almost resolves. It does not.
A second field of noise, minted the same minute, its dots a little warmer and a faint darker shape near the middle that may be nothing.
A third, cooler and greyer, minted in the same transaction.
The fourth, pinker, at a larger size, the lowest number of the four and the only one with a tint you could call a color.
From the second series two days later: fine vertical black and white stripes across the whole square with a few scattered colored dots, sent by the artist to the collector on November 19, 2022.

The Tezos opticals, number one, an animation of twenty-three frames in which a fine black grid on white flickers with dots, minted November 17, 2022 under the GenAI contract and sent to the collector in September 2023.

A field of small marks on white, in rows, like characters on a page seen from too far to read, in fifteen frames that change. The title is kanji, and the artist minted it on Tezos on November 21, 2022, in an edition of twelve, under the contract named GenAI. The collector received it in September 2023, in a batch of four pieces the artist sent to his Tezos wallet within five minutes. A page of writing in no language, from an artist whose last drawings on the board were masks covered in words: the words have gone to marks, and the marks keep the rhythm of a page. It is the quietest thing in the room.

May to September 2023. A scribbled head on Tezos, two cringe-eez doodles on Polygon, a rainbow summer on video and a bar full of skeletons, the last two under a collection whose rules the artist wrote in capitals.

Dark figures in a storm of colored scribble on black, two or three of them, their faces found where the line turns white, their bodies lost in blue and red. It is the scribbled head of the summer of 2022, back on Tezos in May 2023, two months after the drawing board went quiet. The artist sent it to the collector on June 2. In the Faces wing the scribble found friends and then snarls; here it finds a crowd in the dark that has stopped doing either. It is the last work in this collection that looks drawn by the hand that drew the inks.

A head in thin colored line on black, its eyes two rings, its teeth a grille, its hair a scribble of pink and yellow standing up, drawn at four thousand pixels so the line stays thin at any size. The artist called the series cringe-eez doodles and sent the collector two on July 24, 2023, the week after the first numbered mask returned to the drawing board. The title says what it is: a doodle, drawn to be slightly embarrassing, and it is the mask of 2022 drawn with less care on purpose. The artist's bio line on another platform said flawed, imperfect, on purpose. Cringe is the same claim made as a joke.
A second doodle, a skull in green and blue line with a halo of yellow scribble, sent the same day.

A garden under a rainbow sky: trees in blossom, a lawn, a wall of pink and purple cloud, in a tall frame, and it moves, a video of seventy-nine frames in which the light shifts. The artist minted it on Tezos on July 30, 2023, under the GenAI contract, in an edition of twelve, and titled it i send you summer. It came to the collector's wallet in September, with three other pieces in five minutes. The title is a message and the picture is the message: a summer, sent. For an artist who spent a year drawing teeth, it is the least guarded thing in the collection, and the artist used a machine to make it, which the posts of that year say was the point.

A bar full of skeletons and masked figures dancing in a line, painted in orange, green and blue, a crowd that fills a wide frame. It is the first of a collection called GMGL, minted September 14, 2023, whose description reads, in capitals: walk the line until you reach the happy path. Please have all relevant feelings ready when you get there. Take away is not allowed. Violations will be punished with humanity. The artist sent it to the collector the next day. A dance of death in a bar, with instructions: it is the index collection's heaven or hell, a year on, with the hell made cheerful and the rules posted at the door.

November 11 to 15, 2023. Seven flat portraits of men in hats and masks, sent by the artist to the collector's wallet as they were made, and re-issued on a second contract in December, so the collector holds each twice.

A man in a black top hat with a ginger beard and a smiley face for one eye, grinning with white teeth, in a pink shirt, drawn in flat vector shapes against a split ground of blue and green. It is the first Friend of Country Air, a series of seven the artist made in November 2023 and sent to the collector as each was finished. The drawing is clean, flat and cheerful, like the cats of the year before, and the faces are masks again: a smiley over the eye, a grin that is all teeth. Country air is what you take when the city has worn you down. Two years after the drawing board, the artist drew seven men who look like they have taken it.
A yellow mask with a pink band across the eyes and a stalk on top, in a black bow tie and dinner jacket, on blue and olive.
A grey-haired man in a gold crown and yellow glasses with a single tooth, in a white collar on a split ground of tan and teal.
A man in a black hat with hearts for eyes and a stitched mouth, on a split ground of green and blue.
A man in a straw hat with spiral eyes and a yellow mask over his mouth, in a dark coat, on green and cream.
A purple mask with hash marks for eyes and a mouth of fangs, green hair on top, on a split ground of grey and tan, the one Friend that could bite.
An orange hat over green hair that covers the eyes, a moustache and a small mouth, on brown and cream, the last of the seven.
March 19, 2024. The last work in the collection by the artist's own date on any chain: the index collection's fourth piece, a shrine, sent to the collector the hour it was minted.

The inside of a church: a tall gold and blue altar at the end of a nave, light falling from high windows, no one in the pews, in a frame taller than it is wide, and it moves, a hundred and one frames in which the light changes. The artist minted it on Tezos on March 19, 2024, as the fourth work of the index collection, in an edition of one hundred and eleven, and sent one to the collector within the hour. Its title is shrine of create, try, hope, die, and the artist's description reads: insert coin, create, try, hope, die, game over, repeat. It is the last dated work in this collection, from any chain. The artist who began the index collection with a hooded face and the words heaven or hell ended it, so far, with an empty church and the words of an arcade machine. The collector has both. Between them is everything in the rooms upstairs.

The room opens on a face in a hood with the artist's name scrawled over it, published on four chains so it could not be lost, and ends on a shrine with no one in it, titled create, try, hope, die. Between them the artist tried noise, grids, generated light and flat cartoons, and the collector took each one as it came. Heaven or hell, the first title says. The last says game over, repeat, and the shrine is still standing.
